member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraBatch
member.summary: TeraBatch builds one batch command out of all the contained commands and execute it.
member.remarks: TeraBatch will build the underlying commands gradually. It will start with the first command in the list, check if adding another command to the built command will push new command over the database limit. If so, it will summit the existing built command and start over The database limit could be the message size, the number of parameter per request etc. This way, performance will be improved because one round trip of large volume of data is saved.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraBatchMsgSizeCalculator
member.summary:
Estimate if a message has reached its Teradata limit. Message over the limit will cause Teradata to throw an error. The limits are number of parameters for a query, the message size of the request, the size of the sql statement text and the attached data size for the parameters.
A message consists of message header and message body. A message body consists of Option, MultipartRequest, StatementInfo, and KeepResponse parcels. Message header and Options parcel is counted in the overhead. MultipartRequest contains the actual sql text. StatementInfo parcel contains all the parameters descriptions. For a multistatement request, there could be only one StatementInfo parcel, whereas a parameter array request could have multiple StatementInfo parcels.
To calculate the limit for a multistatement batch, the program must first create a TeraBatchMsgSizeCalculator, then keep calling AddCommand until the limit is reached. For parameter array batch the limit is not calculated in advance, so it may result in a DBS Concrete Steps limit error 3714.
member.remarks:
More info in DR 67320.
DBS will throw a 3714 not enough memory to build concrete steps error much earlier than the proposed limit when a multistatement request is used. For a sql request, DBS will parse it into concrete steps and save these step into using row segments (dispatcher segments).
The number of segments for V2R5.0 and earlier is 96. It was increased to 192 in V2R6 and rolled back into V2R5.1. It was increased to 400 in DBS 15.0.4.1. The size of a single segment was originally 64K, including 2K overhead. The size of a single segment in DBS 15.0 is 1MB (may be higher in some cases) unless the entire request is small enough to fit within a 64K segment.
Each segment should hold all the parameters and their descriptions for the steps they contain. However, because of a bug, a segment now holds all the parameters and their descriptions for all the steps in one request. This makes the number of steps a segment can hold much smaller. To calculate how many steps a segment can hold, we need to calculate the datasize of all the parameters and descriptions of all the fields. This will give us the size of one concrete step. Then we can calculate how many concrete steps fit into a single dispatcher segment.
Besides insert, delete or update steps, there may be some other steps. One step for sure to be there is sql step. There maybe a response step, spoil step or replication steps. So we subtract RESERVED_DISPATCHER_SEGMENTS from the dispatcher segment limit to account for these steps.
Example:
Suppose we have a multistatement request with 500 parameters, their using row description size would be 500 * 24 = 12000. Suppose their datasize is 15000. One concrete step requires 12000 + 15000 = 27000 bytes.
For V2R5 and V2R6: The number of concrete steps that can fit in one segment is (64000 - 2000) / 27000 = 2. The maximum number of statements is 96 * 2 = 192 for V2R5.1 and 192 * 2 = 384 for V2R6.
For DBS 15.0.4.1: The number of concrete steps that can fit in one segment is 1048576 / 27000 = 38. The maximum number of statements is 400 * 38 = 15200, which exceeds other limits (like the number of parameters in a query) so it could not be reached.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraCommandStatus
member.summary:
Represents the execution status of TdCommand within a batch.
TdCommand can be in the following status: NotExecuted = TdCommand is still in the queue and not executed yet
Successful = TDcommand is successfully executed.
SuccessfulWithZeroRow = TDcommand is successfully executed but zero rows are impacted. There may be a concurrent update on the same row
Error = Teradata executed the TdCommand and returned an error.
Rolledback = Teradata executed but the result is rolledback because of a later failure

member.summary: Log messages that deal with certain exceptions and other error conditions within Teradata.client.provider and NET. Exception conditions can occur ideally within the scope of known processing exceptions within the code. Developers have provided exception handling to address these exceptions, and the Windows Trace Log will contain indications of the cause that will provide an analyst an initial grasp of how to fix the problem. Central to these kinds of message, stack trace information is provided in the message along with Process Name, EventSourceName (this is the class that a developer would recognize), Timestamp, and Machine Name.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.AppSpecificSwitchLevel.Warning
member.summary: Log messages that need to be communicated to client-support staff and or developer of TDProvider indicating a change of state of some component or class that could cause unexpected results in the system perhaps in the near future. This message ideally indicates where a problem might have initially started, perhaps a database connection that has died, a transaction that did not complete successfully, a Stored Procedure that did not complete, or a command that was not executed on the Teradata Database System.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.AppSpecificSwitchLevel.Info
member.summary: Logs general informational message valuable for determining state of system. This kind of message can gives hints/clues to where the system initial state was before an error or exception occurs. Occurrence of these messages does not indicate a problem or necessarily relate to the problem that Support Staff is attempting to diagnose.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.AppSpecificSwitchLevel.TraceInt
member.summary: .NET Data Provider for Teradata captures Enter Messages and Return Messages corresponding to the internal Teradata.Client.Provider events that developers have placed forth.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.AppSpecificSwitchLevel.Debug
member.summary: Logs messages are specifically designated to accomplish postmortem analysis of the system. Occurrence of these messages does not indicate a problem or necessarily relate to the problem that Support Staff is attempting to diagnose. Ideally, the support staff and/or developer would utilize these messages to gain an understanding of the system prior to the problem occurring (this is where TimeStamp is valuable), whether a LogErrorMessageEvent was raised or not.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.LogEventSource
member.summary: Singleton that represents a Logger Implementation using System.Diagnostics class - LogEventSource.
member.remarks:
LogEventSource implements the interface, "ILog" This enables different logging implementations to be used and determined at build time.
The main components of Tracing for the .NET Data Provider for Teradata are:
An Event Source - The event source is what the developer uses to send tracing messages. Different systems of an application can use different event sources as one way to differentiate the logging/tracing messages.
A Switch - Once a source receives a Log command, it consults its switch to determine whether or not to actually log this message. In this way, by setting a switch higher or lower in a configuration file, a user can regulate which messages are actually logged. The advantage to turning off some trace messages is twofold. Firstly, performance will benefit by not passing through the various tracing code paths. Secondly, in some applications with thorough tracing instrumentation, trace output files can become enormous and difficult to make sense of. Often, it is best to only view the most critical tracing messages and then relax the switch to focus in on a potential issue. Switches in the .NET Data Provider for Teradata use the class "AppSpecificSwitch" for this purpose.
Listeners - Once a switch has verified that a tracing message should, in fact, be logged, the listeners which are attached to the event source will record the data contained in the message. There are many types of listeners and users can even create their own. As with switches, the listeners that are attached to a event source can be determined through a configuration file, allowing excellent run-time control over tracing.
Filters - Listeners can each have a filter attached. A filter is like a switch for a listener. It will determine which trace events are actually processed by the listener. In this way, a user can have multiple listeners attached to a trace source and have each listener record different categories of tracing messages.
Configuration - Configuration files are standard XML files. To turn on different levels of tracing at a client site, the client must provide a TeradataLogging.config file in the current directory. This config file controls the tracing output and writes the output to the specified text log file. Alternatively, logging can be switched on using Logman or PerfView. In this case the trace output is written to the specified *.etl file and can be viewed through PerfView.
One AppSpecificSwitch element is needed for each component/class that is defined in the application.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.LogEventSource._switches
member.summary: Represents Trace Switches from the TeradataLogging configuration file.
member.remarks:
In Teradata.Client.Provider, an entry in class CSwitches corresponds to one or more classes that a developer is interested in tracing and logging.
The TdSwitches array allows developers to reference the LogComponent enumeration when logging a message. This table associates the LogComponent with an Application Switch defined in class AppSpecificSwitch. In the method that accomplishes the logging, the LogComponent enum is used as an index into the TdSwitches array.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.CSwitches
member.summary: CSwitches contains the static instances of the Switches for Logger implementation that is associated with a component or class.
member.remarks:
The Switch corresponds to a class or LogComponent that a TdProvider developer would be interested in tracing or logging. There are predefined AppSpecificSwitch-es for use by developers for logging and tracing in the Teradata.Client.Provider. Note that a developer can add new Switches (see example below) when adding a new class that needs to utilize logging/tracing.
Switches is an array containing BooleanSwitch. LogComponent corresponds to an enumeration of classes in TdProvider that starts with index=0 [MessageData], index=1 [Command], index=2 [Connection] ...
When logging a message, the developer selects the LogComponent corresponding to the class they are working on. This LogComponent is then used in the logger implementation to index the TdSwitches array and reference the correct class within the array. This array of AppSpecificSwitch-es can be added to when adding a new class in TdProvider.
member.example:
To add a new AppSpecificSwitch, say "SomeClass" to Teradata Client Provider a developer would:
1. Add 'internal static AppSpecificSwitch _swSomeClass = new AppSpecificSwitch("SomeClass")' to this file where "SomeClass" is some class that a developer is interested in tracing and logging.
2. Add C# enum that represents this class to internal enum LogComponent. This allows the developer to reference the correct BooleanSwitch via the LogComponent when Logging a message. Example below shows logging a warning message for LogComponent.Connection, which corresponds to class TdConnection:
Logger.Instance.LogWarning(LogComponent.Connection, "TestApp Warning Log!")
3. Add the new LogComponent to the TeradataLogging.config XML file:
false

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcTokenCache.GetStatusAndTokensForScope(Teradata.Client.Provider.UtlConnectionString,Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcParameters,System.String,Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcTokens@)
member.summary: Returns the OIDC token cache status and the cached tokens, if any, for the specified scope.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcTokenCache.GetStatusAndTokensForAllScopes(Teradata.Client.Provider.UtlConnectionString,Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcParameters,Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcTokenCache.Status@,Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcTokens@)
member.summary: Returns the OIDC token cache status and the cached tokens for every scope in the ScopesList.
member.returns: A dictionary where the key is the scope and the value is a tuple containing the cache status and the tokens (if any) for that scope. The output parameter indicates the overall cache status across all scopes, where Miss > Expired > Hit. If any scope is a Miss, the combined status is Miss. If no scopes are Miss but at least one is Expired, the combined status is Expired. If all scopes are Hit, the combined status is Hit. The output parameter returns the tokens for the scope specified in OidcScope used for login.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcTokenCache.GetHashKey(Teradata.Client.Provider.UtlConnectionString,Teradata.Client.Provider.OidcParameters,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a hash key for the specified connection string and OidcParameters using the necessary properties. The IdpUsername serves as the login hint to support multiple identities.
member.remarks: If a UserId is specified for the login hint, then the claim value received from the IdP for the specified OidcClaim is used instead of the UserId.
member.param: The connection string to use for the hash key.
The OIDC parameters to use for the hash key.

If true, the login hint is used as the key. If false, the claim value is used. This is to allow a user to login using an empty login hint, then have the ability to log in using both, an empty string and the login hint that matches the claim value.

It will calculate the scale from the fraction obtained from the TimeSpan structure. The fraction retrieved from the TimeSpan is different in that a fraction with the following values will have the corresponding scale:
FRACTION SCALE 1000000 1 0000010 6 0020000 3 1234500 5 0123450 6

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt160
member.summary:
Supports an unsigned integer that is 160 bits. This will hold the largest number that is supported by the Teradata Number data type. It is only used to operate on the mantissa of the number. It does not deal with the exponent.
Used to support the internal calculations of the Teradata Number Type.
A 160 bit integer is composed of several 32 bit Number Components. A Number Component is an Int32 that when assembled represents the 160 bit integer. There are 5 Number Components in a 160 bit integer. There are high (h), high medium (hm), medium (m), low medium (lm), and low (l) order Number Components. To represent a 160 bit integer, the Number components are assembled in the following order: (h) (hm) (m) (lm) (l)

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt160.AdjustNumber(Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt160,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
A number will be adjusted to the new number of digits indicated by the digits parameters. This will affect the precision of the number.
The number is passed in as a TeraUInt160. ///
member.param: The number of digits to adjust. If the number is positive the precision will be increased by the specified number of digits. It it is negative, the precision of the number will be descreased by the specified number of digits starting with the least significant digit.
The maximum number of digits that can be expected in the result.
member.remarks:
can be either be a positive or negative number. The number passed in for digits will affect both the precision.
Therefore, digits cannot exceed "MaxPrecision – Precision". For example, if the Precision of the number is 20 then digits cannot be greater than 38 – 20 = 18. If digits were greater than 18, the TdDecimal will have a precision greater than the MaxPrecision.
In addition, if a negative value is specified for digits, the absolute value cannot exceed the Scale of the TdDecimal. For example, if the TdDecimal has a Scale of 5, the value of digits cannot be less than -5. A value that is less indicates that the integer part of the decimal (the numbers to the left of the decimal point) is to be either rounded or truncated. AdjustScale does not allow the integer part of the decimal to be rounded or truncated.
Depending upon the value of the parameter, the value will either be rounded to the appropriate number of digits or truncated. If fRound is true, the TdDecimal will be rounded. false the value will be truncated.
member.returns: A 160 bit integer is returned.

When the number is simplified, the adjustment will be reflected in the exponent parameter. Zeros are being removed. So each zero is a power of 10 that is tracked by the exponent.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt160.Multiply160BitInteger(Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt160,Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt160)
member.summary: Multiply two 160 bit unsigned integers
member.remarks:
Multiplication of two TeraUInt160 operands will be performed on each of the number components. The multiplication that is performed is similar to the algorithm when multiplying two based 10 numbers:
888888 x 222222 ------ 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 0 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 0 || 0 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 0 || 0 || 0 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 0 || 0 || 0 || 0 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 8 * 2 || 0 || 0 || 0 || 0 || 0
The "||" is used to separate each of the "one position" of the multiplication operations.
The (8 * 2) calculation is performed and is added the results of the calculations below it --this will be called the "semi-result". Any "overflow" is added to the next "10 based" position. The "overflow" refers to the excess amount that appears in the 10 position or greater.
This algorithm can be expanded. Instead of just using the "one position" of a number to perform the multiplication, the "ten position" can be used:
888888 x 222222 ------ 88 * 22 || 88 * 22 || 88 * 22 88 * 22 || 88 * 22 || 88 * 22 || 0 88 * 22 || 88 * 22 || 88 * 22 || 0 || 0
In this case, the "||" is used to separate each of the "ten position" of the multiplication operation. The "overflow" will appear in the "100 position" of each of the "semi-result". Going from left to right the result of the operation will be:
(88 * 22) + 0 + 0 = 1936 -- 36 (88 * 22) + (88 * 22) + 0 + 19 = 3891 -- 91 (88 * 22) + (88 * 22) + (88 + 22) + 38 = 5846 -- 46 0 + (88 * 22) + (88 * 22) + 58 = 3930 -- 30 0 + 0 + (88 * 22) + 39 = 1975 -- 75 19 result = 197530469136
The algorithm to multiply two 160 bit numbers will be similar. The difference is that the number is separated into 5 number components. A detail explanation of how this is performed in embedded in the code.
member.returns: The 320 bit integer

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt320.CalculatePrecision(Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraInt320)
member.summary: Calculates the number of digits in the 320 bit number.
member.remarks:
The method that is used to determine the precision of a number is to use a binary search of an array. The array consists of values of power of 10 that range from 1 to 96.
A search is performed from the "smallest" power of 10 that is greater than the value. Once this is found the precision can be determined.
The "array" that contains the power of 10's, is actually two arrays. The first 19 values are stored in array of UInt64. The remaining powers are stored in an array of TeraInt320. The reason for this is that it would be much faster to calculate the precision of a value that is less than UInt64.MaxValue using an array of UInt64. There is a lot of overhead when comparing values of TeraInt320.
NOTE: The binary search algorithm is the same when searching the UInt64 array (_digits1to19) and the TeraInt320 array (_digits20to96). Time was spent trying to figure out how to make the search a little more generic so that the same piece of code can be used to search both arrays. However, there is very little code used to implement the search so it was determined it was not worth the extra time to implement common code.
member.returns: Returns the number of digits in the number.

member.remarks:
can be either be a positive or negative number. The number passed in for digits will affect both the precision and scale. The value of digits is added to the Precision and Scale of the TdDecimal.
Therefore, digits cannot exceed "MaxPrecision – Precision". For example, if the Precision of the number is 20 then digits cannot be greater than 38 – 20 = 18. If digits were greater than 18, the TdDecimal will have a precision greater than the MaxPrecision.
In addition, if a negative value is specified for digits, the absolute value cannot exceed the Scale of the TdDecimal. For example, if the TdDecimal has a Scale of 5, the value of digits cannot be less than -5. A value that is less indicates that the integer part of the decimal (the numbers to the left of the decimal point) is to be either rounded or truncated. AdjustScale does not allow the integer part of the decimal to be rounded or truncated.
Depending upon the value of the parameter, the value will either be rounded to the appropriate number of digits or truncated. If fRound is true, the TdDecimal will be rounded. false the value will be truncated.
member.returns: A numbers that contains the result is returned. The adjusted precision and scale are also returned in the out parameters.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDate
member.summary: TdDate is a .Net Data Provider for Teradata specific type that represents a date which is based on the Gregorian Calendar.

remarks.para: The .Net Framework does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the Teradata type Date. Version 1.2 and earlier of the provider map Date to System.DateTime. With the release of version 12.0 of the provider, TdDate is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Date.
The date can range from January 01, 0001 to December 31, 9999.
An application can use the TdDate structure the same way that a System.DateTime is used. TdDate can be used with any version of Teradata supported by the .Net Data Provider for Teradata.

A TdDate can also be specified as an In, Out, or InOut parameter to a Stored Procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider --versions earlier than 12.0--, the Connection String Attribute Enable TdDateTime must be set to false. When this is done, a TdDate is returned to an application using the property. The object that is returned from the property remains a System.DateTime.
If the attribute Enable TdDateTime is set to true a TdDate is returned to the application through the TdParameter.Value.

member.seealso: Date And Time Connection String Attribute
Provider Specific Type: Date And Time Overview

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDate.Add(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: The specified TimeSpan will be added to this instance of TdDate.
member.param: The TimeSpan that will be added.
member.returns: A TdDate is returned that is the result of the TimeSpan added to this instance of TdDate.
member.exception: Unable to add the specified TimeSpan to this instance of TdDate.

remarks.para: If this instance of TdDate is Null a will be returned.

The only component of the TimeSpan object that will be considered is the day component. When this operation is performed, the day component of the TimeSpan is added to the this instance of TdDate. For example, if the date is "2007-10-04" and TimeSpan is "0.02:00:00.00" (0 days, 2 hours) the add operation will result in "2007-10-04".

The number of days will be calculated from the components that were specified when TimeSpan was initialized. Therefore, if a TimeSpan were initialized as new TimeSpan(47, 60, 20) (47 hours, 60 minutes, 20 seconds), the number of days that will be added to TdDate will be 2.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDecimal
member.summary:
Teradata can support decimals that have a precision/scale up to 38. The .NET Framework can only support a decimal that has a scale of up to 28. TdDecimal enables an application to receive and send Large Decimals from and to Teradata. It also contains arithmetic, comparison, and conversion methods that can be used to operate on Large Decimals.
A numeric value between - 10^38 +1 and 10^38 - 1 is supported.

remarks.para: An application can use the TdDecimal structure the same way that a System.Decimal is used. TdDecimal can be used with decimals of any precision/scale and can be used with any version of Teradata supported by the .NET Data Provider for Teradata. However, the maximum precision of the Decimal that can either be retrieved or sent to Teradata is dependent upon the version of Teradata that is being accessed.

A TdDecimal value can also be specified as an In, Out, or InOut parameter to a Stored Procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider --versions earlier than 2.0--, the Connection String Attribute Enable TdDecimal must be set to false, and the precision of the Decimal returned from Teradata must have a precision that is 18 or less. When these two conditions are satisfied, a TdDecimal is only returned to an application using the property. The object that is returned by accessing the property remains a System.Decimal.

If the attribute Enable TdDecimal is set to true or the precision of the Decimal returned from the Advanced SQL Engine has a precision greater than 18, a TdDecimal object is returned from either TdParameter.Value or TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue.

example.para: EXAMPLE 1

The following coding example retrieves Large Decimals from Teradata, modifies the Large Decimal, and then sends the results back to Teradata. The simplified tables that are used in this example have the following definition:
example.code:
CREATE TABLE DetailedSales (TransId INTEGER, RegionId INTEGER, SalesAmt DECIMIAL(38,2))
CRETE TABLE RankSalesByRegion (RegionId INTEGER, TotalSales DECIMAL(38,2), RegionRank INTEGER)

remarks.para: TdDecimal uses four 32 bit integers to internally store the number. The four integers will represent the decimal as a scaled 128 bit integer --the decimal point has been removed by multiplying the number by 10 to the power of the scale. This decimal is stored this way because it is very easy to perform operation on the decimal. The precision and scale are stored separately within TdDecimal.
The four number components that are passed in consist of the following:

list.item: data1 contains the low order bits
data2 and data3 consist of the middle order bits
data4 contains the high order bits

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDecimal.AdjustScale(Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDecimal,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: The scale of the TdDecimal operand will be adjusted to the number of digits indicated by the digits parameter.
member.param: The TdDecimal whose scale will be adjusted.
The number of digits that will be added to the scale and precision.
Indicates whether the number will be rounded after being adjusted.
member.exception: Either the Precision of TdDecimal will be greater than the MaxPrecision, or the integer part of TdDecimal will be affected by this operation.
The new scale will cause an illegal truncation of TdDecimal.
Either the precision or scale is out of Range.
The value of will cause an invalid adjustment to be made.
member.remarks:
can be either be a positive or negative number. The number passed in for digits will affect both the precision and scale. The value of digits is added to the Precision and Scale of the TdDecimal.
Therefore, digits cannot exceed "MaxPrecision – Precision". For example, if the Precision of the TdDecimal is 20 then digits cannot be greater than 38 – 20 = 18. If digits were greater than 18, the TdDecimal will have a precision greater than the MaxPrecision.
In addition, if a negative value is specified for digits, the absolute value cannot exceed the Scale of the TdDecimal. For example, if the TdDecimal has a Scale of 5, the value of digits cannot be less than -5. A value that is less indicates that the integer part of the decimal (the numbers to the left of the decimal point) is to be either rounded or truncated. AdjustScale does not allow the integer part of the decimal to be rounded or truncated.
Depending upon the value of the parameter, the value will either be rounded to the appropriate number of digits or truncated. If fRound is true, the TdDecimal will be rounded. false the value will be truncated.
member.returns: A TdDecimal that contains the result is returned.

The result of this operation will have its set to the maximum scale between the enumerator and denominator. For example, the result of "4 / 5" will be 0. member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDecimal.ToDecimal(Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDecimal)
member.summary: Converts the value of the specified TdDecimal to the equivalent .
member.param: The TdDecimal that is to be converted to a System.Decimal value.
member.returns: A System.Decimal value that is equivalent to the TdDecimal is returned.
member.exception: The TdDecimal value is Null.
The TdDecimal could not be converted to a System.Decimal
member.remarks:
When a TdDecimal has a precision greater than the maximum precision (29) of a System.Decimal it will be converted into a System.Decimal if the TdDecimal can be adjusted so the following are true:
The actual precision of the number will be less than or equal to the maximum precision of System.Decimal.
The Scale will be less than or equal to the maximum scale of System.Decimal
When TdDecimal is adjusted, the fractional part that will not fit into the System.Decimal will be truncated.
The actual precision refers to the precision of the number contained in the TdDecimal structure, not the precision that was specified when creating the TdDecimal. For example, the number 3.8432 has an actual precision of 5 and a scale of 4. A TdDecimal can be initialized with this number with a precision defined as 38 and a scale of 4 using the constructor:
new TdDecimal(38432, 0, 0, 0, 38, 4)
System.Decimal stores numbers as a scaled integer. It can support a number with a maximum precision of 29, maximum scale of 28, and number in the range of minus or plus 79,228,162,514,264,337,593,543,950,335. A scaled integer representation of a number is the number without any decimal separator. For example, the scale integer representation of 43567.90843 is 4356790843. The range of valid numbers also applies to the numbers' scaled integer representation.
Due to these characteristics of a System.Decimal, numbers that have valid precision/scale and are in the valid range may not fit into a System.Decimal. They will need to be truncated one decimal place. These numbers will have an actual precision of 29 and a scale greater than 0. These numbers will also have a scaled integer representation outside the valid range of a System.Decimal. The following are examples of some of these numbers:
Number Scaled Integer Representation
7.9228162514264337593543950336 79228162514264337593543950336
8922816251.4264337593543950335 89228162514264337593543950335
In order to perform a conversion to System.Decimal, these numbers will be truncated one decimal place.
Number To Be Converted Result of ToDecimal Conversion
7.9228162514264337593543950336 7.922816251426433759354395033
8922816251.4264337593543950335 8922816251.426433759354395033
7922816251426433759354959678.5 7922816251426433759354959678
9922816251426433759354395033.2 9922816251426433759354395033

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDecimal.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: Converts the String representation of a number to its TdDecimal equivalent.
member.param: The numeric string that is to be converted to a TdDecimal.
member.returns: The TdDecimal representation of the specified numeric string
member.remarks:
The numeric string that is to be converted to a TdDecimal must have the following format:
[white space][sign]digits.[fractional digits][sign][white space]
The items in brackets are optional. The sign can appear at the beginning of the digits or the end. However it cannot appear at both locations. The digits can also be grouped by a group separator. The number in each group is not checked. However, if a group separator is specified it must be followed by digits. For example,
String Result
1234562546908.23442 is a valid string
1,234,562,546,908.23442 is a valid string
1234,562546,9,08.23442 is a valid string
+1234562546908.23442 is a valid string
1234562546908.23442- is a valid string
-1234562546908.23442- is an invalid string
1,234,562,546,908, is an invalid string
1,234,562,546,908.23,442 is an invalid string
Both the group separator and decimal separator are culture specific.
If the contains the string "NULL" a will be returned.
member.exception: The format of the numeric string is invalid.
The specified numeric string could not be converted to a TdDecimal
The numeric string is null.
member.overloads: Converts a numeric string into an equivalent instance of a TdDecimal.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDay
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in days. The day precision is configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalDay is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Day data type.
The TdIntervalDay supports the Teradata Interval Day (precision) data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the day (from 1 - 4).
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][days]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of days (one to four digits in length).

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Day data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 and earlier versions map Interval Day to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalDay is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Day.
The range of values for each TdInterval precision is as follows:

TdIntervalDay also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalDay structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalDay may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalDay. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the SQL Interval Day data type please see the 'SQL Data Types and Literals' manual.

remarks.para: The number of days is constructed into a TdIntervalDay and validated to determine if the or the values have been exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting days component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalDay(444, 2) requests 444 days with a precision of 2. The resulting days value cannot be represented in 2 digits, therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.
Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDay.#ctor(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a .

remarks.para: The value is converted into a TdIntervalDay and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalDay, any hours, minutes, seconds or microseconds will be truncated. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 9378401234567 results in a value of 10 days, 20 hours, 30 minutes and 40.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalDay literal representation results in a TdIntervalDay value of '10'. The 20 hours, 30 minutes and the 40.1234567 seconds values are truncated. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the day.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToHour
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in days and hours. The day precision is configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalDayToHour is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Day To Hour data type.
The TdIntervalDayToHour supports the Teradata Interval Day (precision) To Hour data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the day (from 1 - 4).
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][days][space character][hh]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of days (one to four digits in length).
Required number of hours from 00 - 23.

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Day To Hour data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 and prior versions map Interval Day To Hour to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalDayToHour is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Day To Hour.
The range of values for each TdInterval precision is as follows:

TdIntervalDayToHour also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalDayToHour structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalDayToHour may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalDayToHour. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the SQL Interval Day To Hour data type please see the 'SQL Data Types and Literals'.

member.summary: An instance of is created from a day and time components specified as integers while precision is specified as a byte.

remarks.para: The number of days, hours and minutes are constructed into a TdIntervalDayToHour to determine if the or the values are exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting days component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalDayToHour(444, 4, 2) requests 444 days and 4 hours with a precision of 2. The resulting days value cannot be represented in 2 digits, therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalDayToHour. For instance, a day value of 200, and an hour value of -4900 will result in a TdIntervalDayToHour interval value of -'4 04'.

member.exception: The parameters specify a TdIntervalDayToHour value less than or greater than .

The precision parameter is not large enough to represent the number of days.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToHour.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a day and time components specified as integers.

remarks.para: The number of days and hours are constructed into a TdIntervalDayToHour and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component.

For example, 99 days and 28 hours is first constructed into a TdIntervalDayToHour. The TdIntervalDayToHour literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToHour value of 100 days and 4 hours within the range of less than or equal to MaxValue and greater than or equal to the MinValue. Precision is calculated to be a value of 3 representing three significant digits in the day.

A day value of 2000 and 200000 hours is first constructed into a TdIntervalDayToHour. The TdIntervalDayToHour literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToHour value of 10,333 days and 8 hours exceeding the maximum value of '9999 23'.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalDayToHour. For instance, a day value of 200, and an hour value of -4900 will result in a TdIntervalDayToHour interval value of -'4 04' with a calculated precision value of 1.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToHour.#ctor(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a .

remarks.para: The value is converted into a TdIntervalDayToHour and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalDayToHour, any minutes, seconds or microseconds will be truncated. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 9378401234567 results in a value of 10 days, 20 hours, 30 minutes and 40.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalDayToHour literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToHour value of '10 20'. The 30 minutes and the 40.1234567 seconds values are truncated. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the day.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToMinute
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in days, hours and minutes. The day precision is configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalDayToMinute is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Day To Minute data type.
The TdIntervalDayToMinute supports the Teradata Interval Day (precision) To Minute data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the day (from 1 - 4).
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][days][space character][hh]:[mm]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of days (one to four digits in length).
Required number of hours from 00 - 23.
Required number of minutes from 00 - 59.

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Day To Minute data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 version and earlier versions map Interval Day To Minute to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalDayToMinute is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Day To Minute.
The range of values for each TdIntervalDayToMinute precision is as follows:

TdIntervalDayToMinute also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalDayToMinute structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalDayToMinute may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalDayToMinute. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the SQL Interval Day To Minute data type please see 'SQL Data Types and Literals'.

member.summary: An instance of is created from a day and time components specified as integers while the precision component is specified as a Byte.

remarks.para: The number of days, hours and minutes are constructed into a TdIntervalDayToMinute to determine if the or the values are exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting days component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalDayToMinute(444, 4, 9, 2) requests 444 days, 4 hours and 9 minutes with a precision of 2. The resulting days value cannot be represented in 2 digits, therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalDayToMinute. For instance, a day value of 200, an hour value of -4900 and a minute value of 30 will result in a TdIntervalDayToMinute interval value of -'4 03:30'.

member.exception: The parameters specify a TdIntervalDayToMinute value less than or greater than .
The precision parameter is outside the or range of values.
The precision parameter is not large enough to represent the number of days.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToMinute.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a day and time components specified as integers.

remarks.para: The number of days, hours and minutes are constructed into a TdIntervalDayToMinute and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component.

For example, 99 days, 28 hours and 75 minutes is first constructed into a TdIntervalDayToMinute. The TdIntervalDayToMinute literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToMinute value of 100 days, 5 hours and 15 minutes within the range of less than or equal to MaxValue and greater than or equal to the MinValue. Precision is calculated to be a value of 3 representing three significant digits in the day.

A day value of 2000, 200000 hours and 0 minutes is first constructed into TdIntervalDayToMinute. The TdIntervalDayToMinute literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToMinute value of 10,333 days and 8 hours exceeding the maximum value of '9999 23:59'.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalDayToMinute. For instance, a day value of 200, an hour value of -4900 and a minute value of 30 will result in a TdIntervalDayToMinute interval value of -'4 03:30' with a calculated precision value of 1.

member.exception: The parameters specify a TdIntervalDayToMinute value less than or greater than .

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToMinute.#ctor(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a .

remarks.para: The TimeSpan value is converted into a TdIntervalDayToMinute and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalDayToMinute, any seconds or microseconds will be truncated. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 9378401234567 results in a value of 10 days, 20 hours, 30 minutes and 40.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalDayToMinute literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToMinute value of '10 20:30'. The 40.1234567 seconds value is truncated. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the day.

member.exception: The timespan parameter specifies a TdIntervalDayToMinute value less than or greater than .

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToSecond
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in days, hours, minutes, seconds and microseconds. The day precision and the second scale are configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalDayToSecond is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Day To Second data type.

The TdIntervalDayToSecond supports the Teradata Interval Day (precision) To Second (scale) data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the day (from 1 - 4) and scale indicates the fractional precision for the values of seconds. The scale may range from 0 to 6.
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][days][space character][hh]:[mm]:[ss].[ffffff]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of days (one to four digits in length).
Required number of hours from 00 - 23.
Required number of minutes from 00 - 59.
Required number of seconds from 00 - 59.
Optionally the number of fractional seconds (0 to 6 digits in length).

remarks.para: The .Net Framework does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Day To Second data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 version and earlier versions map Interval Day To Second to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalDayToSecond is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Day To Second.
The range of values for the TdIntervalDayToSecond containing a day precision of 1 is as follows:

The range of values for day precision values of 2,3 and 4 all follow the same pattern. For completeness, the following chart displays the range of values for a TdIntervalDayToSecond with a day precision of 4.

TdIntervalDayToSecond also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalDayToSecond structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalDayToSecond may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalDayToSecond. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the Teradata Interval Day To Second data type please see the 'SQL Data Types and Literals'.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToSecond.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Byte,System.Byte)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a day and time components specified as integers while precision and scale components are specified as bytes.

remarks.para: The microsecond parameter is divided by 10^-6 (.000001) to create a fractional number of seconds. The supplied scale is used to used to truncate any fractional seconds at the position indicated by the scale.

For example, a microseconds value of 12345678 and a scale of 6 will be divided by 10^-6 and truncated at the 6th position resulting in a value of .123456. A microseconds value of 123 and a scale of 6 will result in a value of .000123.

All values are constructed into a TdIntervalDayToSecond to determine if the or the values are exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting days component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalDayToSecond(444, 4, 9, 2, 90, 2, 6) requests 444 days, 4 hours, 9 minutes, 2 seconds, 90 microseconds with a precision of 2 and a scale of 6. The resulting days value cannot be represented in 2 digits, therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalDayToSecond. For instance, a day value of 200, an hour value of -4900, a minute value of 30, a second value of 400 and 1,200,510 microseconds will result in a TdIntervalDayToSecond interval value of -'4 03:23:18.799490'.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToSecond.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a day and time components specified as integers.

remarks.para: The number of days, hours, minutes, seconds and microseconds are constructed into a TdIntervalDayToSecond and evaluated against and . The microseconds parameter represents 10 ^-6 seconds and the microsecond parameter is divided by 10^-6 (.000001) to create a fractional number of seconds. The is then calculated from the number of fractional seconds required. The is calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component.

For example, 99 days, 28 hours, 75 minutes, 300 seconds and 455666 microseconds is first constructed into TdIntervalDayToSecond and evaluated against MinValue and MaxValue. The TdIntervalDayToSecond literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToSecond value of '100 5:20:00.455666'. Precision is calculated to be a value of 3 representing 3 significant digits of 100 days. The scale is calculated to be 6 from the number of decimal places right of the seconds interval which equals the value.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalDayToSecond. For instance, a day value of 200, an hour value of -4900, a minute value of 30, a second value of 400 and 1,200,510 microseconds will result in a TdIntervalDayToSecond interval value of -'4 03:23:18.799490' with a calculated precision value of 1 and a calculated scale of 6.

member.summary: An instance of is created from a .

remarks.para: The TimeSpan value is converted into a and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval day component and the is calculated from the number of decimal places required to represent the fractional seconds.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into TdIntervalDayToSecond, any fractional seconds will be truncated according the the value of 6 decimal places. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 8726341234567 results in a value of 10 days, 2 hours, 23 minutes, and 54.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalDayToSecond literal representation results in a TdIntervalDayToSecond value of '10 02:23.123456'. The .1234567 seconds value is truncated by one significant digit. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the day.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalDayToSecond, any fractional seconds will be truncated according the the supplied parameter .

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalDayToSecond.Days
member.summary: The number of interval days is returned. The return value ranges from -9999 to 9999.

remarks.para: A is represented as [-][days][space][hh]:[mm]:[ss].[ffffff]. The minus sign is optional and represents a negative interval of time. The days component represents days. The single space character (0x40) separates the days from the hours. The hh represents hours, the mm minutes, the ss seconds and the ffffff fractional seconds. The value of the Days property is the days component.
A negative interval will return all properties (days, minutes, hours, seconds and fractional seconds) as negative values.

remarks.para: Cultural settings are not supported.
The and the number of digits in the most significant field may not match, as the is determined by the number of leading blanks and the number of digits within the most significant field.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHour
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in hours. The hour precision is configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalHour is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Hour data type.
The TdIntervalHour supports the Teradata Interval Hour (precision) data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the hours (from 1 - 4).
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][hours]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of hours (one to four digits in length).

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Hour data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 version and prior versions map Interval Hour to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalHour is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Hour.
The range of values for each TdInterval precision is as follows:

TdIntervalHour also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalHour structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalHour may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalHour. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the Teradata Interval Hour data type please see the 'SQL Data Types and Literals' manual.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHour.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Byte)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a time component specified as an integer while precision is specified as a byte.

remarks.para: The number of hours is converted into a TdIntervalHour and validated to determine if the or the values have been exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting hours component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalHour(444, 2) requests 444 hours with a precision of 2. The resulting hours value cannot be represented in 2 digits, therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.
Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time.

member.summary: An instance of is created from a time component specified as an integer.

remarks.para: The number of hours are converted into a TdIntervalHour and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval hour component.
For example, 99 hours is first constructed into TdIntervalHour. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the hour.
Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHour.#ctor(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a .

remarks.para: The value is converted into a TdIntervalHour and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval hour component.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalHour, any minutes, seconds or microseconds will be truncated. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 9378401234567 results in a value of 10 days, 20 hours, 30 minutes and 40.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalHour literal representation results in a TdIntervalHour value of '260'. The 30 minutes and the 40.1234567 seconds values are truncated. Precision is calculated to be a value of 3 representing three significant digits in the hour.

member.exception: The timespan parameter specifies a TdIntervalHour value less than or greater than .

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHourToMinute
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in hours and minutes. The hour precision is configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalHourToMinute is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Hour To Minute data type.
The TdIntervalHourToMinute supports the Teradata Interval Hour (precision) To Minute data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the hours (from 1 - 4).
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][hours]:[mm].
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of hours from 0 - 9999.
Required number of minutes from 00 - 59.

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Hour To Minute data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 version and prior versions map Interval Hour To Minute to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalHourToMinute is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Hour To Minute.
The range of values for the TdIntervalHourToMinute with hour precision values of 1 - 4 is as follows:

TdIntervalHourToMinute also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalHourToMinute structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalHourToMinute may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalHourToMinute. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the Teradata Interval Hour To Minute data type please see the 'SQL Data Types and Literals' manual.

member.summary: An instance of is created from time components specified as integers while precision is specified as a byte.

remarks.para: The number of hours and minutes are constructed into a TdIntervalHourToMinute to determine if the or the values are exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting hours component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalHourToMinute(444, 4, 2) requests 444 hours and 4 hours with a precision of 2. The resulting hours value cannot be represented in 2 digits, therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalHourToMinute. For instance, an hour value of 20 and a minute value of -4900 will result in a TdIntervalHourToMinute interval value of -'61:40'.

member.exception: The parameters specify a TdIntervalHourToMinute value less than or greater than .
The precision parameter is outside the or range of values.
The precision parameter is not large enough to represent the number of hours.
member.overloads: Initializes a new instance of TdIntervalHourToMinute.
member.param: Number of significant digits of the hour.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHourToMinute.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: An instance of is created from time components specified as integers.

remarks.para: The number of hours and minutes are constructed into a TdIntervalHourToMinute and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval hour component.

For example, 28 hours and 75 minutes is first constructed into a TdIntervalHourToMinute. The TdIntervalHourToMinute literal representation results in a TdIntervalHourToMinute value of 29 hours and 15 minutes within the range of less than or equal to MaxValue and greater than or equal to the MinValue. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the hour.

An hour value of 7000 and 200000 minutes is first converted into a TdIntervalHourToMinute. The TdIntervalHourToMinute literal representation results in a TdIntervalHourToMinute value of 10,333 hours and 20 minutes exceeding the maximum value of '9999 59'.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalHourToMinute. For instance, an hour value of 20 and a minute value of -4900 will result in a TdIntervalHourToMinute interval value of -'61:40' with a calculated precision value of 2.

member.summary: Construct an instance of using a TimeSpan.

remarks.para: The value is converted into a TdIntervalHourToMinute and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval hour component.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalHourToMinute, any seconds or microseconds will be truncated. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 60201234567 results in a value of 0 days, 1 hours, 40 minutes and 20.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalHourToMinute literal representation results in a TdIntervalHourToMinute value of '1:40'. The 20.1234567 seconds value is truncated. Precision is calculated to be a value of 1 representing one significant digit in the hour.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHourToSecond
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in hours, minutes, seconds and fractional seconds. The hour precision and second scale are configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalHourToSecond is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Hour To Second data type.

The TdIntervalHourToSecond supports the Teradata Interval Hour (precision) To Second (scale) data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the hours (from 1 - 4) and scale indicates the fractional precision for the values of seconds. The scale may range from 0 to 6.
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][hours]:[mm]:[ss].[ffffff]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of hours (one to four digits in length).
Required number of minutes from 00 - 59.
Required number of seconds from 00 - 59.
Optionally the number of fractional seconds (0 to 6 digits in length).

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Hour To Second data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 version and prior versions map Interval Hour To Second to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalHourToSecond is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Hour To Second.
The range of values for the TdIntervalHourToSecond containing an hour precision of 1 is as follows:

The range of values for hour precision values of 2,3 and 4 all follow the same pattern. For completeness, the following chart displays the range of values for a TdIntervalHourToSecond with an hour precision of 4.

TdIntervalHourToSecond also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalHourToSecond structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalHourToSecond may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalHourToSecond. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the Teradata Interval Hour To Second data type please see the 'SQL Data Types and Literals' manual.

member.summary: An instance of is created from time components specified as integers while precision and scale components are specified as bytes.

remarks.para: The number of hours, minutes, seconds and microseconds are constructed into a TdIntervalHourToSecond. The microseconds parameter represents 10 ^-6 seconds and the microsecond parameter is divided by 10^-6 (.000001) to create a fractional number of seconds. The supplied scale is used to used to truncate any fractional seconds at the position indicated by the scale.

For example, a microseconds value of 12345678 and a scale of 6 will be divided by 10^-6 and truncated at the 6th position resulting in a value of .123456. A microseconds value of 123 and a scale of 6 will result in a value of .000123.

All values are converted into a TdIntervalHourToSecond to determine if the or the values are exceeded. If the values are not exceeded but the resulting hours component exceeds the supplied value, an exception is generated.

For example a constructor for TdIntervalHourToSecond(44, 6001, 10, 90, 2, 6) requests 44 hours, 6001 minutes, 10 seconds and 90 microseconds with a precision of 2 and a scale of 6. The resulting TdIntervalHourToSecond literal value of '144:01:10.000090' contains an hours value which cannot be represented in 2 digits. Therefore an exception is generated, even though the MinValue and the MaxValue values have not been exceeded.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalHourToSecond. For instance, an hour value of 20, a minutes value of -4900, a seconds value of 30, a microsecond value of 123456, a second precision of 4 and a scale of 6 will result in a TdIntervalHourToSecond interval value of -'61:40:30.123456'.

member.exception: The parameters specify a TdIntervalHourToSecond value less than or greater than .
The precision or scale parameters are outside the minimum or maximum range of values.
The precision parameter is not large enough to represent the number of hours.

remarks.para: The number of hours, minutes, seconds and microseconds are constructed into a TdIntervalHourToSecond and evaluated against and . The microseconds parameter represents 10 ^-6 seconds and the microsecond parameter is divided by 10^-6 (.000001) to create a fractional number of seconds. The is then calculated from the number of fractional seconds required. The is calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval hour component.

For example 100 hours, 75 minutes, 300 seconds and 455666 microseconds is first converted into a TdIntervalHourToSecond and evaluated against MinValue and MaxValue. The TdIntervalMinuteToSecond literal representation results in a TdIntervalMinuteToSecond value of '101:20:00.455666'. Precision is calculated to be a value of 3 representing three significant digits of 101 hours. The scale is calculated to be 6 from the number of decimal places right of the seconds interval which equals the value.

Negative constructor parameters may be supplied to represent negative durations of time. Mixed positive and negative constructor parameters are added together that result in a negative or positive TdIntervalHourToSecond. For instance, an hour value of 20, a minutes value of -4900, a seconds value of 30, and a microsecond value of 123456 will result in a TdIntervalHourToSecond interval value of -'61:40:30.123456' with a calculated precision of 2 and a calculated scale of 6.

member.exception: The parameters specify a TdIntervalHourToSecond value less than or greater than .

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalHourToSecond.#ctor(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: An instance of is created from a .

remarks.para: The TimeSpan value is converted into a TdIntervalHourToSecond and evaluated against and . The is then calculated from the number of digits contained within the interval hour component and the is calculated from the number of decimal places required to represent the fractional seconds.

After conversion of the TimeSpan value into TdIntervalHourToSecond, any fractional seconds will be truncated according the the value of 6 decimal places. For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 368601234567 results in a value of 0 days, 10 hours, 14 minutes and 20.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalHourToSecond literal representation results in a TdIntervalHourToSecond value of '10:14:20.123456'. The .1234567 seconds value is truncated by one significant digit. Precision is calculated to be a value of 2 representing two significant digits in the hour.

remarks.para: This private method is called from all math operations to always set the scale to the scale of the left interval in all operations.
The TimeSpan value is converted into a and evaluated against and . If the values are exceeded an exception is generated.
After conversion of the TimeSpan value into a TdIntervalHourToSecond, any fractional seconds will be truncated according the the supplied parameter .
The precision is set according to the number of digits contained with the field of the TimeSpan * 24 + the field of the TimeSpan.

For example, a TimeSpan value created with a value of 86351234567 results in a value of 0 days, 2 hours, 23 minutes, and 54.1234567 seconds. The TdIntervalHourToSecond literal representation results in a TdIntervalHourToSecond value of ' 02:23:54.123456'. The .1234567 seconds value will truncated by the supplied parameter .
No exceptions are possible because each math operation already validates the result interval for minimum and maximum values.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdIntervalMinute
member.summary: represents an interval of time defining a duration in minutes. The minute precision is configurable.

remarks.para: TdIntervalMinute is a .NET Data Provider for Teradata specific type, designed to support a SQL Interval Minute data type.
The TdIntervalMinute supports the Teradata Interval Minute (precision) data type where precision indicates the number of digits in the minutes (from 1 - 4).
The interval value must be specified in the following format :
[sign][minutes]
Below is the description of each format item.

item.description: Optional - . Defaults as space character (+).
Required number of minutes (one to four digits in length).

remarks.para: .NET does not have a system type that directly corresponds to the SQL Interval Minute data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata Version 13.0 version and prior versions map Interval Minute to System.String. With version 13.1 of the provider, TdIntervalMinute is available to retrieve and manipulate data of type Interval Minute.
The range of values for each TdIntervalMinute precision is as follows:

TdIntervalMinute also supports . This is a very important feature. An application is no longer required to call before invoking the corresponding TdDataReader "Get" method. This will improve overall performance.
A TdIntervalMinute structure allows arithmetic, comparision and conversion operations to be performed.

A TdIntervalMinute may also be specified as an in, out, or in/out parameter to a stored procedure. In order to maintain backward compatibility with previous versions of the provider (release 13.0 and prior), a Connection String Attribute EnableTdIntervals has been added. When the EnableTdIntervals attribute is true, will return the data as the provider specific type of TdIntervalMinute. When EnableTdIntervals is false, TdParameter.ProviderSpecificValue will return the data as a .NET Framework Library data type of .

The will also return the .NET Framework Library data type of System.String when EnableTdIntervals is false to maintain backward compatibility. The TdParameter.Value will return a .NET Framework data type of when EnableTdIntervals is true.
For more information on the Teradata Interval Minute data type please see 'SQL Data Types and Literals' manual.
