member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.AuthenticationMechanism
member.summary: A session security context enabling data encryption and authentication. The following values are supported: BEARER, CODE, CRED, EXTERNALBROWSER, JWT, LDAP, SPNEGO, TD2, TDNEGO.

remarks.para: The .NET Data Provider supports the following session authentication mechanisms: TD2 (Teradata method 2), SPNEGO, LDAP, TDNEGO, and JWT. For a full description of these mechanisms, please reference the Teradata Security Administration chapter on Generic Security Services Library (TDGSS) - Managing Network Security. The default mechanism will be supplied from a client TeraGSS configuration file, if defined, and secondarily from the server's TDGSS configuration file. The default installation of the TDGSS server configuration file sets the value to TD2. The client default TeraGSS configuration file does not set a default value.
For the JWT mechanism, UserId and Password must be null or empty. The format for AuthenticationString is "token=value", where value is the JSON Web Token to be used for authentication.

The .NET Data Provider also supports the following authentication mechanisms that may be used with an OpenID Connect identity provider:
Mechanism Name Description
BEARER
Uses OIDC Client Credentials Grant with JWT Bearer Token for client authentication. UserId, Password and AuthenticationString must be null or empty. JwsPrivateKey and OidcClientId are required. JwsCert is only required for Identity Providers that require an "x5t" header thumbprint. OidcScope, OidcToken and JwsAlgorithm are optional.
CODE
Uses OIDC Device Code Flow, also known as OIDC Device Authorization Grant, for client authentication. AuthenticationString must be null or empty. CodeAppendFile, OidcClientId, OidcScope, OidcToken, OidcPrompt and OidcClaim are optional. If OidcClientId is not specified, the default value configured on the server will be used. If ConnectionPooling is enabled and UserId is provided, the value of the claim specified in OidcClaim must match the UserId. The application may also use the event to display the user code and verification URL for the user to complete authentication.
CRED
Uses OIDC Client Credentials Grant with Client Secret for client authentication. UserId, Password , OidcClientId, and OidcScope must be null or empty. AuthenticationString must contain the Client Credentials Grant request formatted as HTTP POST Form Data encoded as Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded. OidcClaim and OidcToken are optional. The Database user must have the "logon with null password" permission. The Database must be configured with Identity Provider information for Federated Authentication. These tasks are covered in the reference Teradata Vantage™ Security Administration.
EXTERNALBROWSER
The Data Provider will launch the system-browser in order for the interactive user to authenticate with the Identity Provider. This feature must only be used in Desktop applications where a user can interact with the system browser. This feature must not be used in Server-Application scenarios. The Identity Provider must support OpenID Connect, and the AuthenticationString must be null or empty. UserId may be provided for use as the Identity Provider login hint. Password may be used to secure the tokens in the Token Cache. BrowserTabTimeout, OidcClientId, OidcScope, OidcToken, OidcPrompt and OidcClaim are optional. If OidcClientId is not specified, the default value configured on the server will be used. If ConnectionPooling is enabled and UserId is provided, the value of the claim specified in OidcClaim must match the UserId.

Please note that the property is in effect for the Identity Provider authentication process. If the Identity Provider authentication process takes longer than the Connection Timeout value, the connection attempt will fail.
Default Value: Please see the Teradata Security Administration User Manual discussion on the Generic Security Services Library (TDGSS) - Managing Network Security.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.AuthenticationString
member.summary: AuthenticationString supports mechanisms that require additional authentication information.

remarks.para: All mechanisms use this information except for TD2, BEARER, CODE and EXTERNALBROWSER.

The TD2 mechanism only encrypts the logon information and does not perform authentication. The AuthenticationString will be constructed by the .NET Data Provider for Teradata using the UserId and Password properties if the mechanism supports the automatic generation of credentials. If UserId, Password and AuthenticationString have all been specified, the constructed AuthenticationString will consist of a concatenation of UserId@@Password and the original AuthenticationString. This allows an application to specify a UserId and Password and still supply additional authentication data. For examples of Authentication Strings, please reference the Teradata Security Administration chapter on Generic Security Services Library (TDGSS) - Managing Network Security.
If IntegratedSecurity is set to true, any value supplied in this field is ignored.
Default Value: empty string

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.ResponseBufferSize
member.summary: Gets and Sets the initial size of the internal communication data buffers.
member.value: Range of permissible values are from 4096 to 16775168; the default value is 524288.

remarks.para: The Data Provider allocates data buffers for the purpose of receiving data from the Advanced SQL Engine.
The buffer size is adjusted higher when a response message size from the Advanced SQL Engine exceeds the initial size.

The Advanced SQL Engine packs as many rows as possible into a single response message. For example, the Advanced SQL Engine packs 16 rows of size 512 bytes into a response buffer of size 8192 bytes (8192 = 16 * 512).
Refer to Performance Considerations: Response Buffer Size for additional information.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.ReadAhead
member.summary: Enables additional buffering of results, while the current buffer is consumed by an application. This is useful when executing queries that return large result sets.

remarks.para: This behavior is enabled by default. If an application wishes to disable this setting, ReadAhead should be set to false.
Default Value: true

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.MaxDecimalPrecision
member.summary: Used to set the maximum precision of a decimal that can be retrieved from Teradata.

remarks.para: When this attribute is set by an application, Decimal data that is retrieved from Teradata cannot have a precision greater than the specified value.
Teradata V2R6.2 and above support decimal precision up to 38. Versions below V2R6.2 only can support a precision up to 18.
When a connection is going to be made to a V2R6.2 or above version of Teradata the MaxDecimalPrecision can be set to any value between 18 and 38.
When a connection is made to a a version that is below V2R6.2, the MaxDecimalPrecision is ignored. In this situation, the maximum precision of Decimal data that is retrieved is 18.
Default Value: 38

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.UserId
member.summary: The Teradata user id.

remarks.para: If IntegratedSecurity is true, any value in this field is ignored.

For some OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication mechanisms, the UserId is used as the OIDC login hint. If ConnectionPooling is enabled and the UserId is not an empty string, then the UserId must match the claim value returned for the claim type specified by OidcClaim.
Default Value: empty string

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.Password
member.summary: The Advanced SQL Engine password.

remarks.para: If IntegratedSecurity is true, any value in this field is ignored.
Default Value: empty string

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.PersistSecurityInfo
member.summary: The data source object can persist sensitive authentication information such as a password along with other authentication information.
member.remarks: Default Value: false

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.NewPassword
member.summary: Gets or sets a string that contains a new password to be supplied during logons that contain expired passwords.

remarks.para: When the .NET Data Provider for Teradata detects that the original password has expired, it does the following:

list.item: Logs into the Advanced SQL Engine using the original password.
Detects that the original password has expired.
Resets the password using the New Password.
Logs off.
Logs back into the Advanced SQL Engine using the New Password.
Generates an event indicating that password was changed.

remarks.para: When the Data Provider detects that the original password is invalid, it does the following:

list.item: Logs into the Advanced SQL Engine using the New Password.
Generates an InfoMessage event indicating that old password is invalid and the New Password is used.

remarks.para: If the connection string does not specify a New Password and the original password expires, method generates an InfoMessage event with the following message: [Teradata Database] Password has expired, please use MODIFY USER statement to generate a new password
Default Value: empty string

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SessionCharacterSet
member.summary: Gets or sets the character encoding () for the connection.

exception.para: Invalid session character set.

Valid values are: ASCII, ARABIC1256_6A0, CYRILLIC1251_2A0, HANGUL949_7R0, HEBREW1255_5A0, KANJI932_1S0, KANJISJIS_0S, LATIN1250_1A0, LATIN1252_3A0, LATIN1254_7A0, LATIN1258_8A0, SCHINESE936_6R0, TCHINESE950_8R0, THAI874_4A0, UTF8 and UTF16.

remarks.para: The Data Provider encodes Unicode characters to bytes before it sends character data to Advanced SQL Engine. Data Provider also decodes bytes to Unicode characters when it receives character data from the SQL Engine. Data Provider will create an instance of class initialized with Windows Code Page corresponding to Teradata Session Character set as described below.

Data Provider supports the following Session Character Sets and the corresponding Windows Code Pages:
Session Character Set Name Windows Code Page
ASCII ANSI Code page associated with the current thread of execution ().
ARABIC1256_6A0 1256
CYRILLIC1251_2A0 1251
HANGUL949_7R0 949
HEBREW1255_5A0 1255
KANJI932_1S0 932
KANJISJIS_0S 932
LATIN1250_1A0 1250
LATIN1252_3A0 1252
LATIN1254_7A0 1254
LATIN1258_8A0 1258
SCHINESE936_6R0 936
TCHINESE950_8R0 950
THAI874_4A0 874
UTF8 65001
UTF16 1200

the Advanced SQL Engine supports LATIN, UNICODE and KANJISJIS Server Character Sets. UTF8 and UTF16 Session Character Sets are compatible with all Server Character Sets. LATIN1252_3A0 is compatible with LATIN and UNICODE Server Character Sets. KANJI932_1S0 Session Character Set is compatible with UNICODE Server Character Sets. The remaining Session Character Sets are compatible with UNICODE Sever Character Set. ASCII is compatible with LATIN, UNICODE and KANJISJIS as long as character code-points are within the ASCII range.

The KANJISJIS_0S character set includes all the characters in the JIS X 0201 and JIS X 0208 standards, plus extensions, including single-byte Hankaku Katakana characters and multi-byte Kanji characters. KANJISJIS_0S is not 100% compatible with the latest Windows code page 932 as the mapping to Unicode is different for several Japanese characters including the Yen symbol. Therefore, the best practice is to use KANJI932_1S0, UTF8 or UTF16 Session Character Sets with the UNICODE Server Character Set.

The International Character Set Support manual has additional information about Windows compatible session character sets. The manual describes how to enable one or more of the session character sets. Windows compatible session character sets are disabled by default.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SessionMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the Session-Mode.
member.value: Valid values are Default, ANSI and TERADATA.

item.description: The Advanced SQL Engine system default will be used.

In this mode, the Advanced SQL Engine implicitly starts a transaction. However the .NET Data Provider for Teradata immediately commits each Command to simulate Auto-Commit mode required by the ADO.NET specification. The Auto-Commit simulation might add an additional overhead of one (or more for batch-update) round-trip to the Advanced SQL Engine and back.
method must be used to explicitly control the transaction. String comparisons are case specific.
The SQL Engine commits (Auto-Commit) each commands; thus there is less overhead as compared to the ANSI session mode. String comparisons are case insensitive.

remarks.para: Refer to the Advanced SQL Engine manuals for additional information about the ANSI and Teradata session modes.
Default Value: DEFAULT

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.PortNumber
member.summary: Specifies the TCP/IP port number that the .NET Data Provider for Teradata uses for connection to the Teradata Gateway.

remarks.para: You must coordinate changes to this value with accompanying changes on the Gateway.
Default Value: 1025

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.HttpsPortNumber
member.summary: Specifies the HTTPS/TLS port number that the .NET Data Provider for Teradata uses to establish a TLS-encrypted connection to the Teradata Gateway.

remarks.para: This feature is only available with Teradata SQL Engine 16.20.53.30 and above, and TLS must be enabled on the Gateway.
You must coordinate changes to this value with accompanying changes on the Gateway.
Default Value: 443

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.ConnectionPooling
member.summary: Enables or disables connection pooling.

remarks.para: When set to true, actual Teradata sessions are pooled and shared across instances of the TdConnection class. If the pool is empty or a Teradata session is not available, then a Teradata session is created and returned to the application, if the number of sessions does not exceed the MaxPoolSize.
Default Value: True

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.ConnectionPoolingTimeout
member.summary: Specifies the time a connection may stay idle inside the pool.

remarks.para: If a connection stays idle longer than the time specified, and the number of connections exceeds the minimum pool size, the Teradata session is closed and valuable resources are released.
Default Value: 60 seconds

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.MaxPoolSize
member.summary: Maximum number of Teradata sessions allowed in the pool.

remarks.para: Once the MaxPool Size is reached, all requests for new Teradata sessions are queued.
Default Value: 100

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.MinPoolSize
member.summary: Minimum number of Teradata sessions allowed in the pool.

remarks.para: These sessions never timeout and are always active.
Default Value: 0

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.IntegratedSecurity
member.summary: Single Sign On is supported by setting this value. The User Id, Password, and Authentication String values are ignored.

remarks.para: The Account field may still be supplied. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata will choose the AuthenticationMechanism by selecting the highest ranked mechanism configured in TeraGSS that supports SingleSignOn. The application may override this behavior by providing a value for AuthenticationMechanism.

This feature is primarily used on Windows operating system with Active Directory. The Data Provider will utilize SPNEGO authentication mechanism internally. This feature cannot be used with JWT or EXTERNALBROWSER authentication mechanism.
Default Value: false

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.UseXViews
member.summary: All schema queries will return only user owned data.

remarks.para: For example, a tables schema query will access the dbc.tablesx table, in replacement of the dbc.tables table. The dbc.tables table is a system table that may contain many Teradata user id tables, where the dbc.tablesx will contain only a users privately owned tables.
Default Value: true

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.EnableTdDecimal
member.summary: Enables and disables mapping of Decimal(18) to provider specific type.
member.value: Defaults to true. It can be set to false to disable creation of TdDecimal provider specific value type for Teradata Decimal data type with precision less than or equal to 18. It does not affect Teradata Decimal data type with precision greater than 18 (Large Decimal).

remarks.para: will always return TdDecimal type when EnableTdDecimal is set to true. It will return when EnableTdDecimal is set to false and the data returned by the Advanced SQL Engine has a precision less than or equal to 18.

This feature has been added for backward compatibility with older applications. For example an older application, with no need for Large Decimal, might have set to true and later assumed that the resulting columns in are of System.Decimal type.
Default Value: true

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.RestrictToDefaultDatabase
member.summary: Indicates whether Schema queries should be restricted to the Default Database.
member.value: true restricts schema queries to the Default Database. Default value is false.

remarks.para: All Schema Collection queries are restricted to the Default Database () when this property is set to true. The Default Database can be set through the connection string and method.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.DataSourceDnsEntries
member.summary: The number of entries defined in DNS for the DataSource.

remarks.para: The .NET Data Provider will load balance between the DataSource entries found in DNS. The first connection attempt will choose a random number between 1 and DataSourceDnsEntries.
Refer to Data Source Resolution for additional information.
Default Value: -1

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.NodeDownTimeout
member.summary: Obsolete. The number of seconds that must elapse before a connection attempt is made to a node previously marked as unavailable.

remarks.para: NOTE: This API is now obsolete. .NET Data Provider for Teradata uses a new algorithm to detect and bypass down nodes.

As the .NET Data Provider for Teradata load balances across the nodes, a node is marked unavailable if a connection attempt fails. The load balancing algorithm will skip a node that is marked unavailable until the timeout has expired.
Default Value: 900 seconds

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.UseEnhancedSchemaTable
member.summary: Gets or sets a Boolean value that indicates whether method should return additional metadata information (e.g. IsKey and IsUnique).
member.value: The current value of UseEnhancedSchemaTable property, or the default value of true if none has been supplied.

remarks.para: This property controls whether the Data Provider should retrieve additional result set metadata from the Advanced SQL Engine. This feature is available when connected to the Advanced SQL Engine 6.2 or higher.
TdDataAdapter class can use the metadata to set properties and constraints on the DataTable. For example IsKey and IsUnique metadata fields are used to set constraints on a DataTable.
The TdDataAdapter.SelectCommand must return a Key in order for to generate UPDATE, INSERT and DELETE SQL commands now that UseEnhancedSchemaTable is always set to true.
UseEnhancedSchemaTable property must be set to false for backward compatibility with Data Provider version 12.0 or earlier. (The value no longer has any effect on TdCommandBuilder.)
Default Value: true

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.QueryBand
member.summary: Gets or Sets the Query Bands that are to be defined at the Connection Level.
member.value: The current Query Band settings.

remarks.para: This property is used to define Query Bands at the Connection level. Refer to for more information.
The Query Banding feature is available when connected to the Advanced SQL Engine 12.0 or higher.
Default Value: empty TdQueryBand instance

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.Recovery
member.summary: Sets Recoverable Network Protocol (RNP) and Redrive properties used during a network error or database failure.

remarks.para: There are 4 acceptable values:

item.description: Disables RNP and Redrive.
Enables Redrive participation as determined from the Teradata Active System Management (TASM) Redrive setting.
Enables the connection to reconnect in the event of a network error or database failure. Commands may be re-executed and results retrieved after reconnection from a network failure only.

Enables Redrive. The connection will participate in redriving commands after reconnection. Redrive enhances the RNP option, as the Teradata Database spool files are preserved after a database restart when REDRIVE is selected. Commands will be re-executed or restarted automatically from the Data Provider.

remarks.para: Default Value: DEFAULT

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.RecoveryTimeout
member.summary: Recovery timeout in seconds used to re-establish a connection.

remarks.para: The RecoveryTimeout is used if the CommandTimeout is infinite or the RecoveryCommandTimeoutOverride is enabled while the is non-zero.

If the CommandTimeout is 0, the reconnection timeout will always be extended by the RecoveryTimeout value in the application configuration file or the default value if not provided in the application configuration file.

If the CommandTimeout is non-zero, the reconnection timeout will be extended by the RecoveryTimeout value when RecoveryCommandTimeoutOverride is true. Otherwise if the RecoveryCommandTimeoutOverride is false and the CommandTimeout is finite, only the time remaining in the CommandTimeout will be used to reconnect.
Asynchronous commands do not contain or use CommandTimeouts. Asynchronous commands will always use the RecoveryTimeout in reconnection.

The value of the RecoveryTimeout is determined based upon :
The RecoveryTimeout defined here
The RecoveryTimeout obtained from evaluating the ProfileName
The default value

The event enables applications to change the RecoveryTimeout value that has been determined from the above hierarchy. The may be supplied by an application listening for the TdConnection.RecoverConnection event. It will always be activated during recovery in the initial attempt and during subsequent attempts after a calculated delay period. The TdConnection.RecoverConnection event is activated when either of the following is true during reconnection:
CommandTimeout is infinite
CommandTimeoutOverride is true
The command is asynchronous
If the event is activated again because the initial RecoveryTimeout expired, and the application is not listening, no additional time will be provided for reconnection and the reconnection will fail.
Default Value: 1200 seconds

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.ProfileName
member.summary: Specifies the profile name to access the appropriate properties from the application configuration file.

remarks.para: The profile name is used to set the supported properties from the application configuration file during execution. The supported TdConnection.ConnectionString properties are found in the Configuration File Provider Section.

The profile name must exist in the application configuration file. If the profile name does not exist the following error message will be returned - "Invalid connection string attribute: supplied profile name is not a valid value for Profile Name.", preventing a successful opening of the connection.
Default Value: null

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.CommandTimeout
member.summary: This sets the default command timeout.
member.remarks:
The CommandTimeout property represents the amount of time in seconds that the Data Provider waits for a response from Teradata. If the request is not processed within the specified CommandTimeout the request is aborted and the transaction is rolled back. A zero value indicates that the Data Provider should wait indefinitely for the SQL statement to execute.
The CommandTimeout property will be used during Redrive and Recoverable Network Protocol (RNP) support to determine additional time required to support Redrive and RNP. For more details see .
Default Value: 30 seconds

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.RecoveryCommandTimeoutOverride
member.summary: Enables a RecoveryTimeout value to be supplied during reconnection for commands that contain a finite CommandTimeout.

remarks.para: All synchronous commands that contain a zero (infinite) will always extend the reconnection time by the RecoveryTimeout. If the CommandTimeout is non-zero, this new override property (when true) will set the reconnection timeout to the RecoveryTimeout value.
Default Value: true

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.RecoveryStartInterval
member.summary: The starting time interval (in seconds) after which an attempt to retry a reconnection is performed.

remarks.para: The RecoveryStartInterval is used to retry a reconnection that have encountered reconnectable errors. The RecoveryStartInterval is defined as the first time period to wait between unsuccessful efforts to reconnect. It is used to retry reconnection attempts.

The RecoveryIntervalFactor is used to modify the RecoveryStartInterval after the first retry is attempted, by adding the RecoveryIntervalFactor to the initial delay period. Each successive delay period will be modified by the RecoveryIntervalFactor until the delay period exceeds the RecoveryMaximumInterval. The RecoveryMaximumInterval is used to set the upper limit on the calculated delay period, until RecoveryTimeout expires or the reconnection fails.

For example if the RecoveryStartInterval is 2 seconds, the RecoveryMaximumInterval is 16 and the RecoveryIntervalFactor is 2. The delay time between each retry attempt will be calculated as 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 12, 14, 16, 16, 16, etc. If the RecoveryIntervalFactor is 0, the RecoveryStartInterval will be used as the delay period for all retryable attempts, as the RecoveryIntervalFactor will not change the delay period.
Default Value: 2 seconds

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.RecoveryIntervalFactor
member.summary: This represents the adjustment in the recovery interval period from the preceding interval period. The factor is an additive factor in seconds.

remarks.para: The RecoveryIntervalFactor will be added to the RecoveryStartInterval to create a new period of time to delay attempts to reconnect to the Teradata database.

The RecoveryMaximumInterval will limit the upper value of this period of time. For example, if the RecoveryStartInterval is 2, the RecoveryIntervalFactor is 2 and the RecoveryMaximumInterval is 32, the time periods generated internally will be 2, 4, 6, 8, until the maximum delay period of 32 is reached.
Default Value: 2

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.ConnectMaxRetryCount
member.summary: This represents the maximum number of attempts of a retryable error during before an error is returned to the application.

remarks.para: The ConnectMaxRetryCount will set the maximum number of retries for a connection attempt. Once this limit is reached, the connection will fail. For example if the value is set to 200, the Data Provider will retry 200 times before failing the connection attempt and the ConnectionTimeout has not expired.
Default Value: 200

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.RecoveryMaximumInterval
member.summary: This represents the maximum interval time in seconds, used to limit the retry interval time adjusted by the RecoveryIntervalFactor.

remarks.para: The RecoveryMaximumInterval is the maximum interval of time to wait while attempting to reconnect to the database. If a RecoveryIntervalFactor is greater than 0, the RecoveryMaximumInterval will set the upper limit that may be used to delay attempts. When the RecoveryIntervalFactor is 0, the delay will always use the RecoveryStartInterval.
Default Value: 32 seconds

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SslMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the SslMode for connections to the database. SslMode is not used for validating the OpenID Connect Identity Provider endpoint certificates, which are validated using the system default settings.

remarks.para: This feature is only available with Teradata SQL Engine 16.20.53.30 and above, and TLS must be enabled on the Gateway.
NOTE: The Data Provider only checks the certificate revocation status during authentication if SslMode is Verify-Full. The certificate status is not checked with other values of SslMode.

description.para: Disable HTTPS/TLS connections and only connect using the non-TLS PortNumber. If the DataEncryption parameter is set, then TeraGSS is used for encryption.
If the server does not require HTTPS/TLS connections, connect using the non-TLS PortNumber. If the DataEncryption parameter is set, then TeraGSS is used for encryption.
If the server requires HTTPS/TLS connections, establish a TLS-encrypted connection using the HttpsPortNumber.
If the server supports HTTPS/TLS connections, establish a TLS-encrypted connection using the HttpsPortNumber.
If the server does not support HTTPS/TLS connections, connect using the non-TLS PortNumber. If the DataEncryption parameter is set, then TeraGSS is used for encryption.
Establish a TLS-encrypted connection using the HttpsPortNumber.

Establish a TLS-encrypted connection using the HttpsPortNumber and verify that the server certificate is valid and trusted by the Certificate Authority (CA) certificates installed on the client system.

Establish a TLS-encrypted connection using the HttpsPortNumber, verify that the server certificate is valid and trusted by the certificates installed on the client system, and verify that the server certificate contains the DataSource in the Common Name or the Subject Alternative Name. The certificate revocation status is checked for all the certificates, and the connection is terminated if any of the certificates in the certificate chain were revoked. If the revocation status is anything other than revoked or cannot be determined, the behavior is controlled by the SslCRC property.

remarks.para: Default Value: Prefer

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SslCA
member.summary: Specifies the full path and name of a PEM file containing CA certificates. This file may contain one or more trusted root or intermediate CA certificates.
member.remarks: Used for verifying the server certificate.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SslCAPath
member.summary: Specifies the path to a directory containing certificate files in PEM format. The directory will be searched for *.pem files. Each .pem file may contain one or more trusted root or intermediate CA certificates.
member.remarks: Used for verifying the server certificate.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SslProtocol
member.summary: Specifies the minimum version of the TLS protocol for TLS-encrypted connections.

remarks.para: Valid values are null (default), empty string, "TLSv1.2" and "TLSv1.3". Null or empty string allows the Operating System to choose the best protocol.
This setting is ignored for non-TLS connections and for TLS connection to OpenID Connect Identity Provider endpoints on .NET Framework 4.7.1 and earlier.

Setting this property is not recommended. Use it only for testing purposes. Specifying a protocol that is not supported by the Teradata Database or the Operating System will result in error. For example, .NET Framework supports "TLSv1.3" on Windows 11, but not on Windows 10.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.BrowserTabTimeout
member.summary: Specifies the number of seconds to wait before closing the browser tab after Browser Authentication is completed.

remarks.para: The behavior is under the browser's control, and not all browsers support automatic closing of browser tabs. Typically, the tab used to log on will remain open indefinitely, but the second and subsequent tabs will be automatically closed. Specify 0 (zero) to close the tab immediately. Specify -1 to turn off automatic closing of browser tabs.
Default Value: 5

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SslCRC
member.summary: Controls the behavior of the HTTPS/TLS connections to the Teradata Database depending on the result of the certificate revocation check.

remarks.para: NOTE: This setting is ignored when SslMode is not Verify-Full. Additionally, the .NET runtime on Linux only supports the HTTP GET method for OCSP. If the OCSP server only supports the HTTP POST method, certificate validation will fail with errors like RevocationStatusUnknown and OfflineRevocation.

description.para: The connection will be established if the certificate revocation status is not Revoked. The connection will not be terminated if the revocation status cannot be determined or is anything other than Revoked.
The connection will be established only if the revocation status is Good, otherwise it will be terminated.

remarks.para: Default Value: Allow.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.SslCRCTimeout
member.summary: Sets the maximum amount of time to be spent during the retrieval of OCSP response or certificate revocation list (CRL). A value of zero means no limits.

remarks.para: The maximum amount of time taken by the certificate revocation checks in case of slow or unresponsive OCSP or CRL services will depend on the number of certificates that need to be checked and the number of certificate revocation check protocols supported by each certificate.

For example, if (1) the certificate chain contains a leaf certificate, an intermediate CA certificate, and a root CA certificate, (2) the leaf and intermediate both support OCSP and CRL, and (3) the OCSP and CRL services for both certificates do not respond within the specified time, then the total maximum time taken will be SslCRCTimeout * 4 (two OCSP responses plus two CRLs).
NOTE: This setting is ignored when SslMode is not Verify-Full.

remarks.para: A comma-separated list of hostnames that should be excluded from proxying. Asterisks are not supported for wildcards, except a single asterisk may be used to disable the proxy; use a leading dot in case you want to match a subdomain.

Examples: ProxyBypassHosts=.example.com (with leading dot) will match www.example.com, but will not match example.com. ProxyBypassHosts=example.com (without leading dot) will not match www.example.com. ProxyBypassHosts=* will exclude everything. This behavior might be revisited in the future.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.EnableFIPS
member.summary: Enables FIPS mode.

remarks.para: When EnableFIPS is true, the Data Provider will only use FIPS-compliant algorithms for connections to the SQL Engine.
Default Value: false.
This setting does not apply to connections established with OpenID Connect identity providers. FIPS compliance for these connections is dictated by the Operating System.

NOTE: only connections established over SSL/TLS are supported in FIPS mode. Setting SslMode to "Disable" or "Allow" will throw an exception, and the SslMode default value of "Prefer" will be treated as "Require" to avoid establishing non-SSL connections.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.OidcRefreshPercent
member.summary: Specifies the OIDC token minimum remaining lifetime percentage when the token can be reused. The token will be refreshed if the remaining lifetime falls below this percentage.

remarks.para: Default value: 15.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.OidcRedirectPort
member.summary: Specifies the OIDC redirect port number or port number range for Browser Authentication (Authorization Code Flow with PKCE).

remarks.para: This parameter is only intended for use with EXTERNALBROWSER authentication mechanism and is ignored for other mechanisms. Omitting this parameter is recommended.

A null, empty string, or "0" (zero) value directs the Data Provider to use an ephemeral port. IETF RFC 8252 - OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps section 7.3 dictates that an identity provider must allow any port number for the loopback IP redirect URL to let clients obtain an available ephemeral port from the operating system. Only specify this parameter if your identity provider deviates from IETF RFC 8252 and requires a specific port number.
OidcRedirectPort = "port" specifies a single port number for the OIDC redirect URL. The Data Provider will throw an exception if the port is unavailable.

OidcRedirectPort = "portStart-portEnd" specifies a range of port numbers (inclusive) separated by a hyphen. portEnd must be greater than or equal to portStart. The Data Provider will try to bind to each port in the range until it finds an available port. It will throw an exception if none of the ports are available.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.OAuthLevel
member.summary: Controls Single Sign On (SSO) access to Open Table Format (OTF) catalog and storage instances.

remarks.para: If Recovery is not "OFF", the Database supports Control Data and the Database's TASM Redrive setting is enabled, the OAuthLevel specifies which tokens are transmitted to the database with each request, and the database may use the tokens for SSO access to OTF catalog and storage instances. Otherwise tokens are not transmitted to the database with each request, and tokens will not be available for SSO access to OTF.

item.description: (default) disables sending tokens to the database.
Sends the token from OIDC authentication to the database for each SQL request.
Sends the OAuth tokens from OAuthScopes to the database for each SQL request.
Sends the token from OIDC authentication and the OAuth tokens to the database for each SQL request.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnectionStringBuilder.OAuthScopes
member.summary: Specifies one or more OAuth scopes for SSO access to OTF catalog and storage instances.

remarks.para: Multiple scopes are separated by vertical bar characters ('|').
This parameter may only be used with OIDC authentication mechanisms for interactive users, not for service accounts.
This parameter is optional for the EXTERNALBROWSER and CODE authentication mechanisms and must be omitted for the BEARER, CRED, and SECRET authentication mechanisms.

When this parameter is specified, after successful OIDC authentication, the Data Provider obtains an additional access token from the Identity Provider for each specified scope. Each additional access token request uses the same OIDC parameters as the initial OIDC authentication; only the scope is varied.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataAdapter
member.summary: TdDataAdpater fills a DataSet with the data from the Teradata Vantage Advanced SQL Engine and conversely updates the SQL Engine with the data in a DataSet.
member.threadsafety: Any public static (Shared in Visual Basic) members of this type are safe for multithreaded operations. Any instance members are not guaranteed to be thread safe.

remarks.para: The TdDataAdapter retrieves data from the SQL Engine and fills a single DataTable within a DataSet. It is also capable of reconciling changes (UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE) to the DataTable to the SQL Engine.

TdDataAdapter can create the DataTable(s) from SELECT statement's metadata, or it can map the result set(s) to an existing DataTable(s). In either case, data is retrieved from the SQL Engine and inserted / merged into the DataTable. For additional information on naming conventions see DbDataAdapter.Fill method.

TdDataAdapter, working in conjunction with TdCommandBuilder, is capable of automatically generating DML (UPDATE, INSERT and DELETE) statements for reconciling updates to a DataSet. However, UpdateCommand, InsertCommand and DeleteCommand properties can be manually setup as needed or alternatively registered to listen for RowUpdating events and to modify the DML generated by the TdCommandBuilder.

The Data Provider will detect a Parameter declaration discrepancy when Batch Update ( > 1) is enabled and is set to true. The Data Provider detects that the property is set to false but the is set to DBNull.Value. The Data Provider sets the property to true and property to Error # 121007 when it detects this issue. The SQL Engine will detect this discrepancy when Batch Update (UpdateBatchSize == 1) is turned off or ContinueUpdateOnError is set to false. The SQL Engine will return error # 2869.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataAdapter.DeleteCommand
member.summary: Gets or sets a TdCommand used to delete a row from a Teradata Table corresponding to a row in a DataTable..
member.value: Specified a TdCommand object used to delete a row from the Teradata Database table which corresponds to the deleted row in the DataTable. The default value is null.

remarks.para: The DeleteCommand property is used to delete a row from the Teradata Database. The data adapter does not modify the TdCommand object (DeleteCommand) but it maps the DataRow to the TdCommand.Parameters collection and executes the resulting command. See the TdParameter. SourceColumn for additional information on how the columns in the DataTable and how the DataRow are mapped to the parameters.

It is your responsibility to map the columns in DataTable to the parameters. Alternatively, you can use TdCommandBuilder to dynamically generate the TdCommand used to delete a row from the Advanced SQL Engine.
When you set the DeleteCommand property, the TdCommand object passed in is not cloned but rather a reference to the object is maintained by the TdDataAdapter.

member.summary: Add one command to the batch
member.exception: The command parameter passed to the method is not of type TdCommand.
member.returns: number of commands in batch
member.remarks: The command object received from the base class needs to be cloned. The author has designed AddToBatch with an assumption that any Data Provider will/can re-use the command object but change the parameters to match the row that will be added to the batch. However during building a multi-statement request, in BuildToBatch method, the .NET Data Provider for Teradata, clones the first command in the batch and copies the remaining command objects, this eventually leads to ArgumentOutOfRangeException when we calculate the length, bytes written etc for the Parameters in the command object(s). So unless we Clone the command object here, we will be working on the same parameter references leading to the ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdRowUpdatedEventHandler
member.summary: Delegate that will handle the TdDataAdapter.RowUpdated event.
member.param: The source of the event. In this case an instance of TdDataAdatper class.

remarks.para: By the time the RowUpdated event is raised, the changes to a DataRow have been applied to the Advanced SQL Engine. Therefore you cannot affect the current DataRow update, but you can affect the reconciliation of the remaining DataRows. If TdDataAdapter.ContinueUpdateOnError is set to true, then any updates to e.Errors and or e.Status are applied to the DataRow and the TdDataAdapter.Update operation continues. However, if TdDataAdapter.ContinueUpdateOnError is set to false, TdDataAdapter.Update generates an exception and the remaining DataRows are not reconciled back to the Advanced SQL Engine.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdRowUpdatingEventHandler
member.summary: Delegate that will handle the TdDataAdapter.RowUpdating event.
member.param: The source of the event. In this case an instance of TdDataAdatper class.

remarks.para: RowUpdating event is raised before the changes to a DataRow are applied to the Advanced SQL Engine. Therefore you can affect the current DataRow update in addition to the reconciliation of the remaining DataRows

Command, Errors or Status properties of the e parameter can be updated which in turn affects the reconciliation. For example e.Status can be set to System.Data.UpdateStatus.SkipCurrentRow which results in current row not being updated.

If TdDataAdapter.ContinueUpdateOnError is set to true, then any updates to e.Errors and or e.Status are applied to the DataRow and the TdDataAdapter.Update operation continues. However, if TdDataAdapter.ContinueUpdateOnError is set to false, TdDataAdapter.Update generates an exception and the remaining DataRows are not reconciled back to the Advanced SQL Engine.

TdRowUpdatingEventArgs provides data about the event (e.g. SQL statement type like UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE). You can affect the result of the update by setting the Command, Errors and / or the Status property.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader
member.summary: Represents a static forward-only cursor where the individual fields within the current row are accessible using the supported accessor methods.
member.threadsafety: Any public static (Shared in Visual Basic) members of this type are safe for multithreaded operations. Any instance members are not guaranteed to be thread safe.
member.remarks:
TdDataReader does not expose a public constructor and therefore cannot be created by the end-user or application. An application must call the factory method, , to execute a query and retrieve an instance of TdDataReader. TdDataReader encapsulates the data stream returned by the Advanced SQL Engine and exposes the values for each field within a row in addition to column metadata like column name, data type, size and precision.
The SQL Engine supports multiple open result sets per session, allowing multiple TdDataReader objects to be open at the same time. The Advanced SQL Engine supports up to 16 open result sets per session. Once TdDataReader is closed, the corresponding SQL result set is released and resources are freed.
It is highly recommended to close the TdDataReader object. You should not rely on garbage collection because it is nondeterministic, and valuable Server and Client resources would be left open. IsClosed and RecordsAffected are the only properties that you can call after the TdDataReader is closed. All other methods will throw an ObjectDisposdedException.
member.notes:
Teradata can return a row of data in one or more MultipartRecord parcels. A single row can span multiple messages from the Advanced SQL Engine to the Data Provider. Therefore at any single time a TdDataReader can encapsulate the whole row or any portions of it.
TdDataReadere does not cache the data (Parcels). For example a row of data can have zero or more LOBs. Therefore it can conceptually be very large (Gigs of bytes) and cannot be cached within the provider.
TdDataReader has access to all or a limited set of the columns within the row. At any one time it has access to one MultipartRecord parcel. Therefore at any moment it allows access to the range of columns within the parcel. It will throw an exception if the column being accessed is less than lowest column-ordinal within the parcel. For example the parcel might encapsulate data for column 10 to 15. Therefore any request for columns 0 through 9 will result in an exception.
What follows is not the current implementation because of performance considerations; sometimes we have to break OO rules to achieve required performance levels.
For most part TdDataReader can forward the calls to another class like DataReader class. DataReader class process the data stream (parcels) for SELECT statements as oppose to Stored Procedures.
TdDataReader is responsible for CommandBehavior. Based on CommandBehavior and the underlying data stream; it creates one of the DataReader classes like DataReaderStoredProcedure or DataReader. Conceptually one can have DataReader For data returning queries DataReaderDisposed Throws an exception (TdDataReader release the current DataReader and creates an instance of DataReaderDisposed when Disposed is called; which throws an exception.) DataReaderSchemaOnly Only returns Meta data information and throws an exception when GetByte, GetChar and other data returning methods are called.

member.remarks:
Item returns a System.Object that is the root of all types. It is used to retrieve any Teradata data type. The .NET Data Provider for Teradata maps the Teradata data types to .NET Framework types and returns an Object reference.
Item is the most flexible field retrieval method, but is also the slowest field retrieval method. It is strongly recommended to use the other strongly typed field retrieval methods (for example, GetInt32).
This method does not throw an exception for null database fields. It returns an instance of DBNull.

member.remarks:
GetValues is used to retrieve the first N fields where N is less than or equal to the number of columns.
System.Object is the root of all types and therefore can be used to retrieve any Teradata data type. The Data Provider maps the Teradata data types to .NET Framework types and returns references to the .NET Framework instance.
GetValues is the most flexible field retrieval method. However all value types (for example, Int32) are boxed which results in higher resource utilization and are subject to garbage collection.
This method does not throw an exception for null database fields. It returns an instance of DBNull.
GetValues supports sequential access by simply returning the remaining fields. It returns values for fields M through N where M is the last field retrieved plus one and N is either number of fields or the length of , whichever is smaller. For example it would return values for fields 2 through 5 if the first field was already retrieved and there are 5 columns per row.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader.RecordsReturned
member.summary: Gets the number of rows returned from the execution of a SELECT statement.
member.value: The records returned from a select statement
member.remarks:
The RecordsReturned property reflects the activity count of a SELECT statement. The activity count is the number of rows selected. For all other statements this property will be 0.
If the number of rows returned from the execution of select statement overflows Int32.MaxValue, value will be returned. The provider will post an event to when an overflow condition occurs. The event will include a warning code and message. The warning message will have the actual number of records returned. The message code is 114003 and the message text is "An overflow occurred while calculating the number of records returned, actual value is [RecordsReturned]"
NOTE: In order for an application to be aware that an overflow occurred, it must register for the callback with TdConnection.InfoMessage event.
This property is not cumulative. If multiple SELECT statements are contained in a multi-statement request, the RecordsReturned will only contain the activity count of the current result set.

example.para: The following example creates a TdConnection, sets up the TdConnection.InfoMessage event and executes a SQL statement.

When TdDataReader.RecordsReturned is used and if the number of records returned overflows Int32.MaxValue, Int32.MaxValue is returned and a warning message with the actual records returned is exposed through the TdConnection InfoMessage event.

When TdDataReader.RecordsReturned64 is used and if the number of records returned overflows Int64.MaxValue, Int64.MaxValue is returned and a warning message with the actual records returned is exposed through the TdConnection InfoMessage event.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader.RecordsReturned64
member.summary: Gets the number of rows returned from the execution of a SELECT statement.
member.value: The records returned from a select statement.
member.remarks:
The RecordsReturned64 property reflects the activity count of a SELECT statement. The activity count is the number of rows selected. For all other statements this property will be 0.
If the number of rows returned is less than or equal to Int32.MaxValue, both RecordsReturned and RecordsReturned64 properties will return the same value.
If the number of rows returned from the execution of select statement overflows Int64.MaxValue, value will be returned. The provider will post an event to when an overflow condition occurs. The event will include a warning code and message. The warning message will have the actual number of records returned. The message code is 114003 and the message text is "An overflow occurred while calculating the number of records returned, actual value is [RecordsReturned]"
NOTE: In order for an application to be aware that an overflow occurred, it must register for the callback with TdConnection.InfoMessage event. Refer to for an example.
This property is not cumulative. If multiple SELECT statements are contained in a multi-statement request, the RecordsReturned64 will only contain the activity count of the current result set.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader.GetSchemaTable
member.summary: Returns a DataTable that has one row (DataRow) for each column. The rows describe the column metadata.
member.returns: It returns a DataTable for data returning statements (SQL). The DataTable has one row of metadata for each column. It returns null when there is no column metadata.
member.exception: The TdDataReader is closed.

remarks.para: The GetSchemaTable returns the following metadata about each column in the TdDataReader:

description.para: The name of the column which may not be unique. The title of the column is returned if the name is null.
The ordinal (index of array) of the column. Columns are numbered starting from zero.
The maximum possible length of the column in bytes or characters.
Numeric Data Types: This is the size of the data type in bytes (for example, 4 for INTEGER).

Character and CLOB Data Types: The maximum length of the column in characters for LATIN, UNICODE and GRAPHIC. The maximum length of the column in bytes (single-byte character) for KANJI1 and KANJISJIS.
Byte and BLOB Data Types: The maximum length of the column in bytes.
DateTime and Interval Data Types: The maximum length of the column in characters.
JSON Data Type: The maximum length of the column in characters.
NUMERIC Data Types: This is the maximum precision of the column. The range of precision for DECIMAL Data type is from 1 to 38 and it depends on the column definition (for example, Decimal(13,2)).
DateTime Data Types: This is the maximum length in characters.
Interval Data Types: This is the number of digits in the most significant field of the interval. For example a value of '400 10' would contain a NumericPrecision of 3.
All other Data Types: This field is set to 255.
Decimal Data Types: This is the maximum number of digits to the right of the decimal point.
Time, Time With Time Zone, Timestamp and Timestamp With Time Zone Data Types: This is the maximum number of digits to the right of the decimal point.
Interval Data Types: This is the maximum number of digits to the right of the decimal point for all intervals that contain seconds - , , and .
All other Data Types: This field is set to 255.
The .NET Framework data type of the column.
Teradata data type of the column. See TdType Enumeration.

item.description: CLOB, BLOB, XML and JSON Data Types: This column is set to true.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader.Read
member.summary: Advances the data reader to the next record / row.
member.returns: Returns true if the reader is advanced to the next record. Returns false if the end of the result set is reached.
member.exception: The TdDataReader is closed.
The Advanced SQL Engine returned an error, or .NET Data Provider for Teradata detected an error.
member.remarks: TdDataReader is conceptually a static forward-only cursor. Read method advances the current position by one record. When data reader is first created, or when NextResult method is called, the current position is set prior to the first record. Therefore, you must call Read method to get access to the first record and subsequent records. This maintains consistent semantics throughout the interface at all times.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader.GetProviderSpecificValue(System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the value of the specified field (column) as an Object.
member.returns: Returns the value of the specified field represented as a System.Object type.
member.exception: is less than zero or is equal to or greater than or operating in mode and specified column is not accessible.
CommandBehavior is set to SchemaOnly, or there is no data for the row or column, or preceding columns are no longer accessible.
The TdDataReader is closed.
The Advanced SQL Engine returned an error or .NET Data Provider for Teradata detected an error.
member.remarks:
GetProviderSpecificValue returns a System.Object (It is the root of all types) and therefore is used to retrieve any Teradata data type. The Data Provider maps the Teradata data types to .NET Framework types and returns a reference to the .NET Framework instance. It returns and instances when BLOB and CLOB columns are retrieved in deferred mode.
GetProviderSpecificValue is the most flexible field retrieval method and is also the slowest field retrieval method. It is strongly recommended to use the other strongly typed field retrieval methods (for example, GetInt32).
This method does not throw an exception for null database fields. It returns an instance of DBNull.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdDataReader.GetProviderSpecificValues(System.Object[])
member.summary: Gets the value of the specified fields (column) as an Object.
member.returns: Returns the number of fields returned using the object array ().
member.exception: CommandBehavior is set to SchemaOnly, or there is no data for the row or column, or preceding columns are no longer accessible.
The TdDataReader is closed.
The Advanced SQL Engine returned an error, or .NET Data Provider for Teradata detected an error.
member.remarks:
GetProviderSpecificValues is used to retrieve the first N fields where N is less than or equal to the number of columns.
System.Object is the root of all types and therefore can be used to retrieve any Teradata data type. The Data Provider maps the Teradata data types to .NET Framework types and returns references to the .NET Framework instance. It returns and instances when BLOB and CLOB columns are retrieved in deferred mode.
GetValues is the most flexible field retrieval method. However all value types (for example, Int32) are boxed which results in higher resource utilization and are subject to garbage collection.
This method does not throw an exception for null database fields. It returns an instance of DBNull.
GetProviderSpecificValues supports sequential access by simply returning the remaining fields. It returns values for fields M through N where M is the last field retrieved plus one and N is either number of fields or the length of , whichever is smaller. For example it would return values for fields 2 through 5 if the first field was already retrieved and there are 5 columns per row.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdParameter
member.summary: Represents a parameter to a SQL statement.
member.threadsafety: Any public static (Shared in Visual Basic) members of this type are safe for multi-threaded operations. Any instance members are not guaranteed to be thread safe.

remarks.para: Parameterized SQL statements accept one or more input parameters (data). TdParameter represents the data value and can be associated with objects using property. TdParameter describes the .NET data type and the corresponding Teradata column type. The data provider converts .NET data types to SQL data types before it is sent to the Advanced SQL Engine for processing. The data provider cannot derive parameter data type information from Teradata when the TdCommand is prepared. Therefore, the data provider relies on information provided by the TdParameter object or it implicitly maps the .NET data type to Teradata data type.

Teradata Stored Procedures also support output and input-output parameters. TdParameter can correctly map .NET data types to Teradata data types and back and therefore fully support Input, Input-Output and Output parameters to SQL statements.
The data provider does not support the USING CLAUSE. All SQL statements should use parameter markers (Question Mark) as oppose to USING CLAUSE and parameter names prefixed with the colon character.
It is highly recommended to use parameterized queries in order to take advantage of the Teradata Statement-Cache. See the Teradata SQL manual for additional information.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdParameter.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the value of the TdParameter object.
member.value: Specifies an object reference. The default value is null.

remarks.para: For input parameters, the Value property is converted into the TdType before data is transmitted to the Advanced SQL Engine.

The Teradata type is inferred from the Value property if TdType is not specified by the application. .NET primitive data types are mapped and converted to Teradata data types; for example System.Int32 data type is mapped to Teradata INTEGER data type by default. For additional information see Converting Data from .NET to Teradata Data Types.

The data provider uses the IConvertible interface for all non-primitive types assigned to the Value property. The data provider first casts the Value property to IConvertible and then invokes a method corresponding to the Teradata data type (for example: IConvertible.ToInt32). The invariant culture (System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) is used for data type conversions.

To assign a null value (SQL NULL as oppose to null object reference) to a parameter, set the Value property to the System.DBNull.Value property. A null object reference is not the same as System.DBNull. The data provider does not support null object references. Therefore a execution results in an exception if one of the associated properties is set to a null object reference.
The Value property is overwritten if Direction property is set to InputOutput or Output. TdType, Precision, Scale and Size properties are updated to reflect the returned parameter value.

When a BLOB/CLOB is specified as an Input parameter, the Value property must be set to an object that the provider can use to read the data of the LOB. The provider can read the data of a BLOB using one of the following objects:

item.description: Any object that derives from Stream can be used.

remarks.para: When the input parameter is a CLOB, JSON or XML value, the provider can read the data when one of the following type of objects are used:

item.description: CLOB or JSON only. Any object that derives from TextReader can be used.
XML only. Any object that derives from XmlReader can be used.

remarks.para: When a LOB has been specified as an output parameter, a , or will be returned depending upon whether the TdType has been set to TdType.Blob, TdType.Clob/Json or TdType.Xml respectively.
NOTE: If you wish to retreive a LOB output parameter as a String, Stream, Byte[], etc. use the GetValue<T> method instead of using Value.

LOB output parameters maintain their own state, which includes the position within the LOB. The data reader is not able to reset the position to the start of a LOB so you must only call one of the following Properties or Methods, one time:
Value
ProviderSpecificValue
GetValue<T>

remarks.para: The table below defines for each data type:

td.para: Precision is the number of digits before and after the decimal point.
Precision is total number of characters which defines a Date Time data type. For example a value of '1999-05-05 09:20:30.5' will contain a precision of 21.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdParameter.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum size for the transmitted data.

remarks.para:
The Size property is used for binary and string types and has different meanings dependent on the data type:
For non-string data types and ANSI string data, the Size property refers to the number of bytes in the data. This is the case when the property is set to DbType.AnsiString, for example.
For Unicode string data, the Size property refers to the number of characters in the string. This is the case when the DbType property is set to DbType.String or the TdType property is set to TdType.VarChar or TdType.Clob.
The Size property is ignored for XML output parameters.

When creating a parameter for a character array or a string, the application programmer must be cognizant of the Session Character Set used for logging on to the Advanced SQL Engine. It is important to understand when to specify the number of bytes or the number of characters.

For example, if a column in a table is defined with the server character sets Kanjisjis or Kanji1, any parameters that refer to these columns must have the DbType property set to DbType.AnsiString. The value of Size must represent the number of bytes of the string to be sent to Teradata.
The following are descriptions of additional scenarios and their expected behaviors:

Scenario: A table that contains a column defined as VARCHAR(20) CHARACTER SET KANJISJIS. The DbType has been set to DbType.AnsiString, the size of this column is defined in bytes (please refer to the "SQL Reference: Data Types and Literals" for more information). The Session Character Set has been set to UTF16. The character array has a length of 8 and contains only ASCII data.

Expected Behavior: Each character in the array will take two bytes of space after being encoded into the UTF16 Session Character Set. If the Size property has been set to 4, then only two characters of the array will be sent to Teradata. If the Size has been set to 20, all 8 characters will be sent.

Scenario: A table contains a parameter declared as VARCHAR(64000) CHARACTER SET LATIN, and the session character set has been set to UTF8. In the application, the DbType is set to DbType.String or DbType.AnsiString and the character array contains ASCII characters. The Size has been set to 32,001.

Expected Behavior: The Advanced SQL Engine will return an error indicating that the column or character expression is larger than the max size. This is because the maximum size of a VarChar literal in a Unicode session character set is 32,000 characters. There are several ways to avoid this problem:
Specify a Session Character Set that has a fixed-byte number of bytes per character of 1, if possible.An example of such a character set is ASCII.
Use a data type that supports a larger size. For example, set the TdParameter.DbType property to TdType.Clob.
Scenario: The Session Character Set has been set to UTF16. The DbType has been set to DbType.AnsiString. The Size has been set to an odd value.

Expected Behavior: The Advanced SQL Engine will return an error about a malformed character. In this scenario, the Size must be a multiple of the minimum character length in bytes. Since the minimum character length in bytes for a UTF16 character set is 2, Size must always be an even value.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdParameter.TeraTypeBaseCache
member.summary: Implements the caching strategy to be used by the GetTeraTypeBase method. method.
member.remarks:
THe GetTeraTypeBase method uses a design strategy pattern to return either a cached or a non-cached TeraTypeBase value.
The strategy is selected when the _teraTypeBaseDelegate is initialized to: a) non-caching (default) strategy: TdParameter.GetTeraTypeBaseNoCache b) caching strategy: TdParameter.TeraTypeBaseCache.GetTeraTypeBaseCache
The caching strategy is used in the following scenarios: 1) If the Parameter was created internally by TdStream to execute "SELECT ?" and retrieve a LOB. The "SELECT ?" query is executed internally by TdStream.ExecuteReader() and TdStream.OpenAsync(). In these cases we must create an internal output parameter to hold the result of the query. We call an internal constructor TdParameter(TeraTypeBase value) and pass a TeraTypeBase instance, like TeraTypeBlobLocator and TeraTypeClobLocator. We do not set _value, _precision, _scale, etc. This internal constructor selects the caching strategy. 2) To improve performance of Multi-Statement Batch, which accesses the same TeraTypeBase value from different methods sequentially. The IsEligibleForParameterArray() method selects the caching strategy.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdParameter.InitializeWithoutCache
member.summary: Initializes the TeraTypeBase to enable TdParameter reuse. Uses a non-caching strategy.
member.remarks:
If TdDataAdapter.ContinueBatchOnUpdate is set to True and an error occurs during batch execution, some commands from the batch may need to be resubmitted. Before these commands may be resubmitted, TeraTypeBase must be re-initialized, because some if its fields were modified during the initial command execution and may not be reused when the command is resubmitted.
With this strategy, TeraTypeBase is not cached and re-initialization is not required.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdParameter.InitializeWithCache(Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeBase)
member.summary: Initializes the TeraTypeBase to enable TdParameter reuse. Uses a caching strategy.
member.remarks: With this strategy, TeraTypeBase is cached, and multiple calls to GetTeraTypeBase() method will return the same TeraTypeBase instance. If a new instance of TeraTypeBase is desired, such as when a failed batch command must be recreated and resubmitted, this method must be called again to create a new TeraTypeBase instance.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdTransaction
member.summary: Represents an Explicit SQL Transaction. It should be explicitly committed or rolled back.
member.threadsafety: Any public static (Shared in Visual Basic) members of this type are safe for multithreaded operations. Any instance members are not guaranteed to be thread safe.
member.remarks:
By default object operates in Auto-Commit mode. Therefore the transaction spans the execution of one or more object. The application can open a transaction via and explicitly control when the transaction is committed or rolled back.
the Advanced SQL Engine will rollback a transaction when a SQL statement results in a specific set of errors. In this case, the .NET Data Provider for Teradata will open a new explicit transaction and the TdTransaction object can be used to commit or abort the remaining activities associated with the object.
The object reverts back to Auto-Commit mode after an explicit call by the application to
or method.
Unlike the ODBC Driver and OLE DB Provider for Teradata, the .NET Data Provider for Teradata does not automatically commit a transaction after a DDL statement execution. Therefore, the DDL statement has to be the last SQL statement within a transaction. Furthermore the DDL statement cannot be part of a multi-statement request.
member.internalremakrs:
The internal Constructor will issue a Begin Transaction as needed (ANSI mode does not require a begin transaction).
Upon failure an Explicit transaction is restarted. It is the users responsibility to call Commit or Rollback.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TdTransaction.ReStartTransaction(Teradata.Client.Provider.TdConnection)
member.summary:
When an SQL fails (Failure parcel as oppose to error parcel) in Teradata Mode, the transaction is rolled back. To be consistent with ODBC and OLE DB, We will start a new transaction ("Begin Transaction") and continue the work. The exception will indicate that work up to that specific point has been rolled back. However the explicit transaction is still in place and have to be committed or rolledback.
TdCommand will trap the exception and call this method (Note per ADO.NET TdCommand has to have a reference to the transaction). The method will start a new explicit transaction.
Note that all this work is for Teradata Session Mode and not ANSI Session mode. Also note that Teradata accepts multiple Begin Transaction commands however the transaction is only commited after the last ET.
member.param: connection associated with the TdCommand; used for validation
member.exception: Thrown if parameter cn is not equal to the TdConnection associated with this instance
Throw if transaction cannot be restarted; note the object will be in disposed/Zombie state if TdException is thrown.

member.summary: The Transaction Level Query Bands are modified to those defined in .
member.param: The Query Bands that will be defined at the Transaction Level.
member.exception: Query Bands or Trusted Sessions are not supported by the Advanced SQL Engine.
Transaction is not opened.
is null.

remarks.para: Query Bands are only supported when connecting to a Teradata Database 12.00 or later releases.
When this method is called, a "SET QUERY_BAND ... FOR TRANSACTION" statement is submitted to the Advanced SQL Engine. The old settings are removed, and the new settings are created.
The Transaction Level Query Band is set to NONE when the input parameter has Zero ( is equal to zero) Key-Value pairs.
The Query Bands that have been defined at the Connection level are still active during the transaction.

summary.para: Represents an object (i.e. Parameter) whose data type is defined at runtime. It is conceptually similar to a Variant type.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.ConnectionFactory
member.summary:
Encapsulates access to the instances of Connection resource. It follows the singleton pattern. Therefore Instance field is used to access the one and only instance of ConnectionFactory.
ConnectionFactory is responsible for: 1- Pooling Disabled a- Create a Connection object b- Open a session to Teradata c- Returns the connection Note: All work is done by ConnectionPool.CreateConnection method.
2- Pooling Enabled a- Find the ConnectionPool by looking up the ConnectionString b- Request a Connection from the pool c- returns the connection to caller

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.ConnectionPool._activeConnections
member.summary: Connections that are recently returned to the pool. When timer goes off, they are moved to _agedConnections. Synchronized access to active connections.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.ConnectionPool._agedConnections
member.summary: Set of connections that are candidate for removal from the pool. When timer goes off, all connections in _agedConnections are removed and disposed. Next all connections in _activeConnections are moved to _agedConnections. The sum of connections in _aged and _available is considered the total number of available connections.

member.summary: Set of all connections created by this pool. Reference keeps the connection from being garbage collected. During cleanup an orphaned connection is returned to _activeConnection.

member.summary: Keeps track of how many connections are left in the pool. It starts off by allowing for maximum number of connections. Connections are created on demand and later released back to the pool (_activeConnections).

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.ConnectionPool.OnProcessExit(System.Object,System.EventArgs)
member.summary: Close all socket connections to the SQL Engine when Process is existing.
member.remarks:
.NET Core does not guarantee Finalization when process is exiting. This means that WpSocket.Dispose will not be invoked and Pooled connections to the SQL Engine will not be cleaned up.
We also need it on .NET Framework, because SslStream may get disposed before we can send the LogOff request.
This event will try to logoff the Session to the SQL Engine and close the stream and the socket connection.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.Metadata
member.summary: Holds Metadata for Columns or Parameters.
member.remarks:
PrepInfoX and DataInfoX parcels return Column metadata for a statement. StatementInfo parcel returns Column and Parameter metadata for a statement.
Conceptually DataInfoX has least amount of Metadata followed by PrepInfoX and StatementInfo parcels.
We use the Metadata classes as to bridge the differences between the three parcels mentioned above. We want most of the code to be dependent on Metadata set of classes but not PrepInfoX, DataInfoX or StatementInfoX.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.Parcel
member.summary:
Represents an abstract Teradata Parcel. A Teradata parcel is made up of Type, Length and Body (bytes). The Parcel Type is also known as FLAVOR (i.e. ParcelFlavor see above enum). The Parcel Type indicates what has been serialized into the Body. Please see CLI manual for the description of how to interpret the body.
Teradata wire-protocol support two Parcel formats; namely Parcel and Alternate Parcel Header (APH). Basically APH increases the body size from 64K to 1MB.
Parcel Format: Flavor is 2 Bytes long Length is 2 Bytes long Body is x Bytes long where x = Length - 4
Alternate Parcel Header: Flavor is 2 Bytes long Reserved is 2 Bytes long Length is 4 Bytes long Body is X Bytes long where x = Length - 8
Parcel class abstracts the differences between APH and old Parcel format.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.Parcel.BeginWrite(Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelWriter)
member.summary: Saves the current position of the parcel writer and sets the position of the writer to where the parcel body should start in the buffer.
member.remarks: This method is primarily needed for CLOBs but is also used with BLOBs. The contents of the CLOB is written to the body of the parcel before the parcel header is written. This is necessary because the actual byte count of a CLOB cannot be calculated until after all the characters of the CLOB that will fit within a parcel has been written to the buffer. After the parcel body has been filled, the position of the writer is set to point the position of the header, then the parcel header information is written (Parcel.WriteParcelHeader).

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelReader
member.summary:
Conceptually very similar to System.IO.BinaryReader. It reads data from parcel body and keeps track of current position.
Read methods don't do boundary checks. Read methods have to perform well; therefore it is the responsibility of the caller to perform such boundary checks.
IMPORTANT ********************** Note: Internally a BitConverter is used to read from the buffer. BitConverter takes the endianess into account. Therefore it correctly reads from little and big endian data streams. It assumes that the data stream matches the computer architecture.
