member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelWriter._bytesPerCharacter
member.summary: Stores the number of bytes per a character after being encoded
member.remarks:
The purpose for this object is that the bytes per character is calculated by calling the method Encoding.GetMaxByteCount. This method returns a byte count that includes bytes for one extra character. The reason for this is stated on Shawn Steele's blog at http://blogs.msdn.com/shawnste/archive/2005/03/02/383903.aspx. The two reason he states why this is necessary are:
1. One reason for this oddity is that an Encoder could store a high surrogate on one call to GetBytes(), hoping that the next call is a low surrogate. This allows the fallback mechanism to provide a fallback for a complete surrogate pair, even if that pair is split between calls to GetBytes(). If the fallback returns a ? for each surrogate half, or if the next call doesn't have a surrogate, then 2 characters could be output for that surrogate pair. So in this case, calling Encoder.GetBytes() with a high surrogate would return 0 bytes and then following that with another call with only the low surrogate would return 2 bytes.
2. Another change is that GetMaxByteCount(n) now asks the fallback what the worst case for an unknown character is. So if I have a fallback that looks like new EncoderReplacementFallback("{Unknown Character}"), then those 19 characters will be aggravate our worst case. For 1252, GetMaxByteCount() would then be 19 * (n + 1), or 38 for GetMaxByteCount(1)!
We will never encounter these two problems when handling character data. Therefore, it will be save to subject off the bytes for the extra character. In order to do this, we will need to know how many bytes is needed to encode a character. This will be done by
Encoding.GetMaxByteCount / 2

member.summary: Re-hydrates a Parcel from the byte array (buffer) into an appropriate object. Note when MoveNext is called the position within the buffer is advanced but the actual parcel object (e.g. PclSuccess) is not created until GetParcel is called. This is a very important feature. It allows for skipping specific parcels. For example in a multi-statement request, one can skip from one statement to the next.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelFactory.ReadAheadScan
member.summary: Scans the current buffer looking for a PclEndRequest or a PclError/PclErrorInfo parcel and saves the information. Resets the buffer back to the beginning. This is only called from BeginRead() so we should always be at the beginning of the message buffer. This was done so that we don't have to scan twice, once looking for the PclEndRequest and again for the PclError parcel if it is at the end of the buffer.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclErrorInfo
member.summary: It holds a 4-byte response buffers size.
member.remarks: Error Parcel has a 2-byte info fields. It usually indicates the response buffer size. However when response exceeds 64K, the Error.Info property cannot hold the required response buffer size. Teradata will send a 3177 error code in Error Parcel followed by a ErrorInfo parcel. The parcel body is variable length; {Id, Length, Info} fields can repeat within the body. However at this point there is only one Id; Id of 1 indicates a 4 byte response buffer size. So this is what we expect: Id = UInt16 set to 1 Length = UInt16 set to 4 Info = UInt32 has the response buffer size.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclMultipartRecord.BindColumns(Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeBase[],System.Boolean,System.UInt32,System.UInt32@,System.Boolean@)
member.summary:
One needs a map (DataInfoX or PrepInfoX) to decipher MultipartRecord parcel. However, it is actually harder than that; a single MultipartRecord parcel might not contain all columns. It even can contain partial column data. Therefore the binding provides information on: 1- Which column(s) might reside in this parcel. 2- Whether this is the first parcel or not; First parcel carries the indicator fields for all columns.
This method calcs the offsets for fields/columns within this parcel. It returns the range of columns that it can return data for and whether the last column is continued on to the next parcel.
Conceptually A single MultipartRecord parcel would provide data for all columns if there are no LOBs. Therefore the bind should provide access to all columns.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclOptions._spReturnResult
member.summary: Indicates if the response should be returned to the sender of the request and/or the caller/client
member.remarks:
Valid only for version 12.0 or later. The possible values for this field are:
0 -- the default, indicates the response should be returned to the stored procedure 1 -- the response should be returned just to the client 2 -- response returned just to the caller of the stored procedure 3 -- response should be returned to the client and the stored procedure 4 -- response should be returned to the caller of the stored procedure and the stored procedure.
For client applications this field should always be set to 0.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclOptions.PARCEL_BODY_SIZE
member.summary: Options Parcel body size.
member.remarks:
For Teradata version earlier than v12, the actual length is 10. For Teradata version 12 the actual length is 11. For Teradata version 13.10 the actual length is 15. For Teradata version 14.0 the actual length is 16. For Teradata version 14.10 the actual length is 17 for XML. For Teradata version 16.0 the actual length is 21 for large rows. For Teradata version 20.0.x the actual length is 22 for VSD Catalog Name.
However, The Teradata Database is designed to ignore EXTRA BYTES. Therefore we do not have to selectively, based on DBS Version, write out the options. The Data Provider will always write out the Maximum Number of Bytes as indicated by this constant.

This parcel is both send to Teradata and received from Teradata.
The parcel is send to Teradata when SQL has parameterized queries. It precedes the PclIndicData parcel.
The parcel is send to Client to describe the record parcel. We usually use the PrepInfo parcel but in some cases (Create Procedure) we have no choice but to use the DataInfo to describe the record parcel.

member.summary:
Binds the parameter values to the MultipartIndicData Parcel.
The assumption here is that the parameters specified by the application can be divided into an arbitrary number of parcels. For example if application specifies 10 parameters, then maybe 2 is placed in the very first parcel 3 parameters in the second parcel with the last parameter continuing on to the next parcel 1 parameter in third parcel 5 parameters in the last parcel.
First parcel will carry the NULL Indicator bits.
member.param: Encapsulates the parcel writer; Used to calculate the wire-size of Char data types

Whether this is the very first parcel (NULL Indicator bits).
Max Parcel Size in bytes. Limits how many parameters will be persisted to the buffer
The last parameter that will be persisted to the parcel.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclConfigResponse._supportsStatementIndependence
member.summary:
Statement Independence.
Indicates that the version Teradata allows statements to fail in a multi-statement or iterated request without rolling back the implicit transaction. This is only supported when the request only contains INSERT statements --as of Teradata 13.10.
The provider only supports Statement Independence from the TdDataAdapter. It will be invoked when connected to a Teradata 13.10 or greater release and TdDataAdapter.ContinueOnUpdate is set to true.

member.summary: Unity Attributes added. This includes additional Client Attributes, such as PCLCLIATT_CLIENT_IPADDR_BY_CLIENT (31), PCLCLIATT_CLIENT_PORT_BY_CLIENT (32), PCLCLIATT_SERVER_IPADDR_BY_CLIENT (33), PCLCLIATT_SERVER_PORT_BY_CLIENT (34) and PCLCLIATT_COP_SUFFIXED_HOST_NAME (45).

member.summary: Indicates that the version of Teradata supports Enhanced Statement Status (ESS).

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclConfigResponse._supportedESSLevel
member.summary:
Teradata support for ESS is implemented in phases. - A value of 0 from Teradata would indicate ESS is not supported. - A value of 1 indicates support limited to replacement of success/OK parcel (along with 8 byte activity count), inclusion of single warning message self-defining extension.
A feature Teradata release would support replacements for Error/ErrorInformation, Failure and StatementError parcels. As additional phases of ESS are deployed, the level set indicator would be incremented.

This was introduced beginning with the 14.10 release. Within the control data block is the Security Parcel that is used to centralize the security features of Teradata. The provider will read this parcel to determine the following: SecurityRequired ConfidentialityRequired securityLevel

member.summary: Item Layout carries information about this Type. For example if Layout is Full and Content is Parameter, then we are receiving Parameter Metadata from DBS.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclStatementInfo.ItemLayoutLimitedContent
member.summary: Encapsulates the Wire-Representation of "Limited Content Item layout". This layout is a replacement for DataInfo and DataInfoX parcels.
member.remarks: Field Data Type Description ------------------- -------------- ------------------------------------------- Item Layout Type 2 byte integer Must be set 2. Item Content 2 byte integer Must be set to 8 for sending Parameter Data to DBS. Item Length 2 byte integer Length of the item body. It does not include the header (Layout Type, Content and Length). Data Type 2 byte integer Data Type Code (i.e. TeraType ENUM values). Max data length 8 byte integer Max Data Length in bytes. Numeric Digits 2 byte integer Total number of digits for numeric data types. Otherwise it is set to zero. Interval Digits 2 byte integer Some Interval data types have Max precision. For example INTERVAL YEAR(n) where n is a number between 1 and 4. Fractional Digits 2 byte integer Number of fractional digits for Numeric (Decimal) and Interval Data Types.

member.summary:
Indicates whether parcel extensions follow the fixed length part of the parcel. 0 indicates that no extensions follow. 1 indicates that self-defining extensions follow.
As of 14.10, no extensions have been defined, so this field will always equal 0.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclSecurityPolicy.SecurityRequired
member.summary:
Indicates that Teradata requires that the buffer that is sent to Teradata must be secure.
This may mean that the buffer must either be encrypted or have integrity verified. When the buffer is encrypted it includes integrity.
If this is true, the client at a minimum must ensure integrity.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclSecurityPolicy.ConfidentialityRequired
member.summary: Indicates that Teradata requires that the client must encrypt the buffer.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclSecurityPolicy.SecurityLevel
member.summary:
The minimum level of security that was specified by Teradata.
The provider will just specify this level when securing the buffer.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclSecurityPolicy.SecurityPolicyExtension

As of 14.10, Teradata does not use the extension.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclMultiIndicDataGroup
member.summary: This class represents a pseudo-parcel that is responsible for managing/writing one or more of the MultiIndicData and EndMultiIndicData parcels.
member.remarks:
This calls is used to write several parcels out to the buffer. If the Teradata database supports SLOBs, the parcels that will be written as follows: MultiIndicData SlobStart Ordinal or LOB column -- starts from 1 SlobData LOB Data SlobDataEnd ... (additional Slob parcels) EndMultiIndicData ... (repeat MultiIndicData...EndMultiIndicData)
When LOBs can only be sent to Teradata as inline or deferred, the following parcels will be written: MultiIndicData EndMultiIndicData ... (repeat MultiIndicData...EndMultiIndicData)
When parameter array are used, this pseudo-parcel will continue to write MultiIndicData parcels until either all the parameters have been processed or when the message buffer has been filled. Once a message buffer has been filled, it is sent to Teradata for processing. If there are rows that have not been processed, the processing of building the message buffer is performed again. This will continue until all the rows have been processed.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.PclMultiIndicDataGroup.LobKey.CompareTo(Teradata.Client.Provider.PclMultiIndicDataGroup.LobKey)
member.summary: The comparer class that is used to sort the LOBs by size when the LOB TeraType has been added to the SortList.
member.remarks:
It is used in the DetermineLobInLine method to determine which LOB can be in-lined.
The LOBs are sorted in ascending order based on ActualSize. The smallest LOBs will be in-lined first if there is enough room in the parcel.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.RequestState
member.summary:
Valid Request Object states: Active = Request sent to Teradata and awaiting a response.
ElicitingData = Teradata responded with ElicitData parcel, requesting additional data for BLOB and or CLOB.
Succeeded = Teradata responded with Success parcel, meaning the the request finished executing and spool is ready to be retrieved.
Failed = Teradata responded with Failure parcel and Transaction is rolled back.
Errored = Teradata responded with Error parcel and transaction is not rolled back.
Aborting = Abort was sent to Teradata. Note that application should wait for a response from Teradata to see if abort succeeded.
Closed = Spool file is cleaned up and discarded.
Positioning = Requesting additional rows from Teradata.
State Transition: Active to ElicitingData, Succeeded, Failed, Errored, Aborting ElicitingData to Active, Aborting Succeeded to Aborting, Closed, Positioning Failed to Closed Errored to Closed Aborting to Succeeded, Failed, Errored?? Closed to Positioning to Succeeded

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.SynchronizationState
member.summary:
The state the synchronization objects are currently in. Undefined -- No commands are being processed
Begin -- A command has initiated processing. It is going through the sync objects to access the session
End -- The command has completed processing and is releasing the session.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.Request
member.summary:
Represents a pending request to Teradata. The Request class makes use of various WpMessageManager classes to accomplish request actions (e.g. Start Request, Continue, Abort, Cancel). The WpMessageManager classes encapsulate the message protocol.
When the object is first created, a Teradata-request is initiated. The request is placed in Active state. Clients to this class can execute requests and provide a timeout limit for the request to complete. At any time Clients can issue an abort and therefore stop the long running query. For additional information see RequestState and each method's summary.
SYNCHRONIZATION NOTES: To enhance performance, this class relies on higher layers to provide locking. That is TdCommand should lock the TdConnection before any further calls to Request or Connection class. This provides a single point of locking and will enhance overall performance.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.Request.NextResultSet(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Advances the ParcelFactory to the next result set (SUCCESS parcel).
member.remarks:
A Message Gate controls access to the session. when a Start Message passes through the gate, the status of the gate will be changed to CLOSED.
When moving through the result set, a Continue Message will be sent to Teradata to retrieve another buffer full of data. This message is sent by GetNextBuffer().
Normally, an attempt to send a message when the Message Gate is shut will generate an "busy session" exception. However, when a ExecuteNonQuery is called to execute a SELECT, the provider must process the rows returned. A Boolean parameter to MoveNext is specified to indicate that the thread will wait for the Message Gate to open if it is currently closed.
member.returns: true if there are more result sets; false otherwise.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.Request.NextResultSetAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asynchronously advances the ParcelFactory to the next result set (SUCCESS parcel).
member.returns: a Task result of true if there are more result sets; false otherwise.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.Request.FindNextSuccessParcelInBuffer(Teradata.Client.Provider.PclError@)
member.summary: Advances the ParcelFactory to the next Success or StatementError parcel in the current buffer.
member.param: The error parcel if we find one
member.returns: true if the parcel was found; false otherwise.
member.remarks:
A StatementError parcel will only be returned when Statement Independence has been turned on. Currently, the provider will only turn on statement independence when the TdDataAdapter is being used to batch requests.
Teradata will only use Statement Independence when the batch that consists of all INSERT statements. Otherwise, it will handle the batch in the "usual" way. It behaves this way even when Statement Independence has been turned on by the provider.
A StatementError parcel will not cause the provider to throw an exception. It is used to indicate that a statement in the batch failed. The provider will update the data table with the error.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.Request.BeginTransmit(Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession.MessageType,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Used to start the transmission of Messages to Teradata. Method will check the status of the Message gate and wait on EventHandle until it has been set.
member.param: The message type that is going to be submitted
indicates that caller wants to wait for the Message Gate to open: true==wait for open, false==busy exception will be thrown
member.remarks:
The message types are as follows: NoopMessage -- no messages StartMessage -- start message AbortMessage -- abort message OtherMessage -- other type of messages not including start and abort.
There is a scenario where an exception will NOT be thrown if the Message Gate is closed. This will occur when a Continue Message is sent going through the result set of a SELECT that was executed by BeginExecuteNonQuery/ExecuteNonQuery. In this case, the thread sending the Continue Message will wait until the Message Gate is open. This is indicated by setting the waitForMsgGateOpen parameter to true.
waitForMsgGate = true is only applicable to an Other Message.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.Request.EndTransmit
member.summary: Ends the transmission of Messages to Teradata. It signals the EventWaitHandles to let another thread access the session, and will open the Message Gate.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeClob.BeginWrite(Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelWriter)
member.summary: Calculate the maximum and actual length.
member.remarks:
TeraTypeBase.ActualByteLength
In this TeraType the ActualByteLength property is used differently than the other TeraTypes. Because of performance reasons the ActualByteLength contains the maximum number of bytes that will be written with the **Offset** taken into account. This differs from TeraTypeBase.MaxByteLength in that MaxByteLength is the total number of bytes of the string/char array.
If ActualByteLength were to contain the actual length of the string/char array, then ParcelWriter.GetByteCount would be called. This method scans the string to calculate the length. This has a tremendous negative impact on performance.
We can get away with setting ActualByteLength to the "maximum number of bytes to write", because the ActualByteLength is eventually used to calculate the maximum number of bytes that a Multi-Indicator Data parcel will use.
member.param: Parcel writer encapsulates the session character set.

member.summary: Encodes the Unicode data into the session character set.
member.returns: number of bytes written to the buffer.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeClobDeferred
member.summary: Implements type information and conversion, Encode and Decode for Teradata Clob Column.
member.remarks: Deferred LOBs are different than other data types. When all the input parameters are written out to the IndicData parcel, a UID is written out for deferred LOBs. The database receives the UID, and sends back an ElicitData parcel. At this point Teradata is ready to receive data of the corresponding LOB. The data is sent to Teradata using one or more MultiData parcels.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeJsonDeferred
member.summary: Implements type information and conversion for Teradata Json Parameter.
member.remarks: Deferred LOBs are different than other data types. When all the input parameters are written out to the IndicData parcel, a UID is written out for deferred LOBs. The database receives the UID, and sends back an ElicitData parcel. At this point Teradata is ready to receive data of the corresponding LOB. The data is sent to Teradata using one or more MultiData parcels.

It also maps TeraType to TdType, DbType and .NET Type
TeraType TdType DbType .NET Type Comment ============= ============== ===================== ============== ================== VarChar VarChar AnsiString String Char[] Alternate Mapping
Char Char AnsiStringFixedLength String Char[] Alternate Mapping
VarByte VarByte Binary Byte[] Max 64000 bytes
Boolean Not Supported
Byte Byte Binary Byte[]
Currency Not Supported
Date Date Date DateTime Time portion is set to 00:00:00.00
Timestamp Timestamp DateTime DateTime
Decimal Decimal Decimal Decimal
Double Double Double Double
Guid Not supported
SmallInteger SmallInt Int16 Int16
Integer Integer Int32 Int32
BigInt BigInt Int64 Int64
Object Not Supported
ByteInteger ByteInt SByte Int16
Double Double Single Single
VarChar VarChar String String Max 64000 characters (depends on target column)
Char Char StringFixedLength String Max 64000 characters
Time Time Time TimeSpan
UInt16 Not Supported
UInt32 Not Supported
UInt64 Not Supported
VarNumeric Not Supported
Blob TdBlob Binary Byte[] Max 2GB (user to explicitly set TdType and not DbType) Stream
Clob TdClob String Char[] Max 2GB (user to explicitly set TdType and not DbType) String TextReader
Graphic Graphic StringFixedLength String Max 64000 (user to explicitly set TdType abd not DbType)
TimeWithZone TimeWithZone String String (user to explicitly set TdType and not the DbType)
TimestampWithZone DateTimeOffset TimestampWithZone DateTimeOffset
VarGraphic VarGraphic String String (user to explicity set TdType and not the DBType)
PeriodDate PeriodDate String String
PeriodTime PeriodTime String String
PeriodTimeWithTimeZone String String PeriodTimeWithTimeZone
PeriodTimestamp PeriodTimestamp String String
PeriodTimestampWithTimeZone String String PeriodTimestampWithTimeZone

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeFactory.GetTeraType(Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraType,System.Int32,System.Byte,System.Byte,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSessionContext,System.Data.ParameterDirection,System.Object)
member.summary:
Create an instance of TeraTypeXXXX class based on TeraType and TeraExtType parameters. The TeraTypeXXXX class can later be used to persist data to a data parcel (MultipartIndicData or IndicData).
Conceptually this maps a TdParameter to TeraTypeXXXX class. TerTypeXXXX class is responsible for data conversion. TeraTypeXXXX will throw an exception if it does not support the conversion requests by the application. For example if application passes a DateTime value but sets the DbType/TeraType to Int32. TeraTypeInt will use Convert.ToInt32 which results in InvalidCastException.
member.param: Teradata data type; see TeraType Enum.

Maximum size of the column. For Char and Varchar this refers to the number specified at table creation (e.g. Char(15), Char(5)). However, per specification the size is in number of characters when DbType is set to String or StringFixedLength; but size is number of bytes when DbType is set to AnsiString. Size is also used for Binary, Byte and is number of bytes.
Max number of digits for Decimal, Time and Timestamp.
Number of digits to right of decimal point for Decimal, Time and Timestamp
Used for client-side chunking of LOBs.
Indicates TeraType was derived from DbType
Only used when TeraType varchar/char. Indicates that size is in bytes
Contains information about the session -- TeraConfig, connection string, Session info.
value/data to be send to Teradata
member.returns: A TeraTypeBase object.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeDecimal
member.summary: Implements type information for Teradata Decimal.
member.remarks:
Note that Teradata returns the precision and scale as length. PrepInfoX has a 64 bit length while PrepInfo has a 16 bit length. Constructor will take this into account.
TeraTypeDecimal support 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 bytes Decimals. Wire protocol is a scaled integer. For example 12.24 is scaled to 1224. The scale is send to client in PrepInfoX parcel.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeVarChar.BeginWrite(Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelWriter)
member.summary: Calculate the maximum and actual length.
member.remarks:
TeraTypeBase.ActualLength
In this TeraType the ActualLength property is used differently than the other TeraTypes. Because of performance reasons the ActualLength contains the maximum number of bytes that will be written with the Offset taken into account. This differs from TeraTypeBase.MaxLength in that MaxLength is the total number of bytes of the string/char array.
If ActualLength were to contain the actual length of the string/char array then ParcelWriter.GetByteCount would be called. This method scans the string to calculate the length. This has a tremendous affect on performance.
We can get away with setting ActualLength to the "maximum number of bytes to write" because the ActualLength is eventually used to calculate the maximum number of bytes that a Multi-Indicator Data parcel will use.
member.param: Parcel writer encapsulates the session character set.

member.summary: Actual column size; for example VarChar(2000) might have an actual size of 100.
member.remarks:
In TeraTypeVarchar the ActualLength property is used differently than the other TeraTypes. Because of performance reasons the ActualLength contains the maximum number of bytes that will be written with the Offset taken into account. member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeBase.SetCurrentUnitLength(Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelReader)
member.summary: Set CurrentUnitLength based on actual data and number of bytes.
member.remarks:
Teradata returns number of bytes for CHAR, VARCHAR and CLOB data types. We have to perform a pre-flight and calculate number of Characters based on actual data.
Most other data types use bytes for units. for example BYTE data type returns CurrentLength for CurrentUnitLength.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeBase.SetParcelBindings(System.UInt32,Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelWriter)
member.summary: Given a Max number of bytes to write to the parcel, TeraType calculates whether it can write all data (SQL Parameter) or not. LOBs can be split across multiple parcel using this scheme. That is a single LOB can be written into multiple MultipartIndicData parcels. Each parcel can be transmitted via a separate message. Therefore, in general TeraTypes are capable of splitting their data across multiple messages going to Teradata.
member.param: Max number of bytes to write to the parcel
Encapsulates the Encoding for Character data types. Encoding is used to calculate the number of bytes
member.returns: True if it can write to parcel; false otherwise.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeLobWrapper
member.summary: TeraType that is used as a base class for wrappers for the LOB types.
member.remarks:
The wrappers are used to wrap the Deferred and "In-Lining" types of a LOB. If the data of a LOB can be included in the data sent to the Teradata database, the wrapper will instantiate the In-Line type of the LOB. However, if the LOB is too large it will be sent using deferred mode and will instantiate the deferred TeraType of the LOB.
When a wrapper is created, the default type that is initially created is the deferred teratype of the LOB. When it is determined a LOB can be included in the MultiIndicData parcel, the "in-line" type will be instantiated.
The "in-line" type is used when the LOB data is in-lined in the parameter data or the data is sent as a SLOB.

member.remarks: This field is only use when SLOB is not supported by the Teradata database.

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeLobWrapper._maxByteLengthForOptimization
member.summary: A LOB will not be optimized if the Size is greater than the value of this field.
member.remarks:
Is set to SessionContext[SessionLimits.MaxBytesRequest].
For CLOB and XML, the Size (TdParameter.Size) represents the number of characters. If the MaxByteCount of the Size were calculated it will be greater than or equal to the Size. Therefore, if the Size is greater than or equal to this field, it cannot be optimized.

member.remarks: The characteristics that will enable a LOB to be optimized are the following: Size greater than max request buffer size Size != 0 and Value is not a TextReader, XmlReader or Stream.
member.param: The maximum space allocated for one parameter row.
member.returns: true -- is a candidate to be optimized, false -- cannot be optimized

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeLobLocator
member.summary: Implements type information for Teradata LOB Locators.
member.remarks:
Note that there are two locators namely Blob and Clob locators. Teradata sends locators to the Provider. Provider later will use the locator to retrieve the LOB. Provider executes "Select ?" and passes the locator to DBS. Therefore TeraTypeLobLocator can read and write to the stream (wire-protocol).
Note that a locator is much like a VarByte; that is PrepInfo/DataInof has the max length. Actual length is in MultipartRecord / Record parcel.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeDateInteger
member.summary: Supports receiving Integer Date from DBS. It does not send Integer Date to Teradata.
member.remarks:
Application can set Session DATEFORM to integer after logon (TdConnection.Open) by executing the following DDL statement:
SET SESSION DATEFORM=INTEGERDATE
DBS will send a 4-byte signed integer to client using the following formula: (YEAR - 1900) * 10000 + (MONTH * 100) + DAY
Note that DBS sends ANSI Date as CHAR(10) with 'YYYY-MM-DD' format; therefore integer date has the added benefit of removing 6 additional bytes.
Provider will receive Integer Date and map it to System.DateTime or TdDate. This feature helps applications that refuse to use ANSI DATE literals; also DBS will apply 'YY/MM/DD' format for to new Tables in INTEGERDATE mode.
We have received lots of request from SQL-Assistant users with legacy scripts; now they can establish the connection, change to Integer Date Form and then execute legacy scripts.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeXmlWrapper
member.summary: This is the base class for all the wrappers for the LOBs.
member.remarks:
The wrappers are used for optimization of the LOBs.
There are two TeraTypes for each type of LOB -- deferred TeraType and a In-Line TeraType. In-Line infers that the data of a LOB will be written to the message buffer either In-Lined in the MultiIndicData parcel or as a SLOB parcel(s).
The wrappers enable switching between the two TeraTypes of a LOB. When a Wrapper is created, it is initialized with the Deferred type. If it is determined that the LOB can be optimized, the underlying type is switched to the "In-Lined" type.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.TeraTypeXml.BeginWrite(Teradata.Client.Provider.ParcelWriter)
member.summary: Calculate the maximum and actual length.
member.remarks:
TeraTypeBase.ActualByteLength
In this TeraType the ActualByteLength property is used differently than the other TeraTypes. Because of performance reasons the ActualByteLength contains the maximum number of bytes that will be written with the Offset taken into account. This differs from TeraTypeBase.MaxLength in that MaxLength is the total number of bytes of the string/char array.
If ActualByteLength were to contain the actual length of the string/char array then ParcelWriter.GetByteCount would be called. This method scans the string to calculate the length. This has a tremendous affect on performance.
We can get away with setting ActualByteLength to the "maximum number of bytes to write" because the ActualByteLength is eventually used to calculate the maximum number of bytes that a Multi-Indicator Data parcel will use.
member.param: Parcel writer encapsulates the session character set.

summary.para: Normalize DataTable select data by replacing all embedded single quotes with 2 single quotes.

The DataTable select filter statement uses TableName and ColumnName to select unique rows from the table. The single quote character may be in the data as it is valid as a character in Teradata object names, but is not valid in the filter statement without escaping.

member.param: Object name (e.g. Table Name) to normalize.
member.returns: Normalized DataTable select data.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.UtlSqlParser.IsSQLValidCallStmt(System.String)
member.summary: This method validates if the input commandText is a syntactically correct CALL statement. It does not validate (in entirety) if the object names in the CALL statement are valid Teradata DBS object names.
member.returns: True if the commmandText is a syntactically correct CALL statement, false otherwise.
member.remarks: A valid CALL statement can be as follows: 1) Start with keyword CALL (assuming there are no comments at the beginning) 2) Followed by object name (quoted, unquoted, hexadecimal literal string, unicode delimited identifier) 3) Optionally followed by a qualifier (.) and object name 4) Followed by open parenthesis 5) Followed by zero or more object names separated by commas or parameter markers 6) Followed by closing parenthesis 7) Optionally followed by semi-colon at the end of the string (assuming no comments at the end)

item.description: Unencrypted, and the application does not have the option to change this during the session.
Not applicable to .NET Data Provider.
TDGSS used for encryption, and the application does not have the option to change this during the session.
TLS was attempted, but failed, so this is a fallback to using TDGSS for encryption because ENCRYPTDATA is specified.
TLS was attempted, but failed, so this is a fallback to unencrypted because ENCRYPTDATA is not specified.
TLS used for encryption. Server certificate was ignored; client did not validate the identity of the server.
TLS used for encryption. Client validated the Certificate-Authority chain but ignored the Subject-Alternative-Name and the Common-Name.
TLS used for encryption. Client validated the Certificate-Authority chain and the Subject-Alternative-Name or the Common-Name.

member.summary: Dictionary defining the retry-able and reconnect-able errors.

remarks.para: These errors are always mapped to TdException error numbers. Any socket errors are caught and mapped to a TdException error that will be retry-able or reconnect-able.

The concept of retry-able and reconnect-able are one in the same, and the methods contains different signatures for determining if an error may be retried. The true value indicates that the error is retry-able.

While some retry-able and reconnect-able errors may be caused by transient network errors, such as those caused by a server restart, the errors related to TLS and the dual port connection strategy indicate that the connection used the wrong port and can be retried immediately. returns false for such errors.

member.summary: An asynchronous timer used to reconnect any asynchronous failures.
member.remarks: During reconnect operations, this timer is created from OnContextReceiveComplete or OnContextSendComplete. This timer is created to free the OS Callback thread and to continue retrying a reconnection until the reconnection is successful. This occurs when the retry-able errors have transitioned to reconnect-able errors. Each time the timer is invoked, the previous timer method is returned back to the thread pool.

member.summary: Creates an execution context.
member.returns: An ExecutionContext

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.ExeContextType
member.summary: The execution context types.

remarks.para:
OpenConnection IRetry Class - RetryFixedIntervalMaxRetry INotify Class - RNPNullNotify IFault Class - FaultStrategyInitialConnect or FaultStrategyInitialConnectDualPort The retry interval is fixed and the retry stops after a maximum number of retries. The connection timeout is still used to stop the connection attempt. There is no notification using the TdConnection Recovery event.
Uses : This execution context is used in Connection Open

DefaultRetryFaultNoNotify IRetry Class - RetryFixedIntervalMaxRetry INotify Class - RNPNullNotify IFault Class - FaultStrategyReconnect The retry interval is fixed and the retry stops after a maximum number of retries. There is no notification using the TdConnection Recovery event.
Uses: Development and Testing

DefaultRetryFaultNotify IRetry Class - RetryFixedIntervalMaxRetry INotify Class - RNPNotify IFault Class - FaultStrategyReconnect The retry interval is fixed and the retry stops after a maximum number of retries. There is notification using the TdConnection Recovery event.
Uses: Default Request execution context

MultiplyIntervalRetryFaultNotify IRetry Class - RetryVariableInterval INotify Class - RNPNotify IFault Class - FaultStrategyReconnect The retry interval is using the RecoveryFactor as a multiplier when calculating a new retry interval. There is notification using the TdConnection Recovery event.
Uses: Development and Testing

AdditionIntervalRetryFaultNotify IRetry Class - RetryVariableIntervalFixedFactor INotify Class - RNPNotify IFault Class - FaultStrategyReconnect The retry interval uses the RecoveryFactor as an additive modifier to the retry interval. There is notification using the TdConnection Recovery event.
Uses: Development and Testing

FixedRetryNoFaultNoNotify IRetry Class - RetryFixedIntervalMaxRetry INotify Class - RNPNullNotify IFault Class - FaultStrategyNoReconnect The retry interval is fixed and the retry stops after a maximum number of retries. There is no notification using the TdConnection Recovery event and no reconnect support from the IFault interface.
Uses : The WpTestManager uses this context.

Off - WpSession is returned. with no context. Uses: WpConfigManager, WpAssignManager, WpAuthMethodsManager, WpSecurityManager, WpLogonManager, WpLogoffManager, WpCancelRequestManager, WpAbortRequestManager, HelpSession from WpSession.Open, TdConnection ExecuteQueryBandStmt from TdConnection.Close, TdConnection SetSessionIsolationLevel from TdConnection.Close, TdConnection Rollback from TdConnection.Close,

member.summary: WpSecurityManager manages the wire protocol for the Assign and SSO message exchange.

Since that is the only difference between V2R6.0 and pre-V2R6.0, the logic was left in one WpSecurityManager. The other major difference in the releases is how the mechanisms are selected. member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpRequestManager.CheckForBufferOverflow(System.AsyncCallback,System.Object)
member.summary: Checks the response for a Buffer Overflow condition
member.returns: True if we have sent another continue request to resize the buffer asynchronously
member.remarks:
1- Error Code 3115, 3116 and 3177 handled by Message Managers: a. WpRequestManager.CheckForBufferOverflow method: It will resize the Response Buffer and send another Continue Message when the first Parcel in the very First Response is Error Parcel with error code 3115, 3116 or 3177.
i. WpStartRequestManager.ProcessRequestResponse method: it invokes CheckForBufferOverflow. Note that this method is eventually used for Synchronous and Asynchronous SQL Execution.
ii. WpStartRequestManager.ProcessDeferredResponse method: It invokes CheckForBufferOverflow after it sends all Deferred Parameters (LOBs). This instance of CheckForBufferOverflow handles Synchronous SQL Execution. The Asynchronous SQL Execution with Deferred Parameters case is still handled in ProcessRequestResponse.
iii. WpContinueRequestManager.ProcessContinueRequest method: It invokes CheckForBufferOverflow method to resize the Response Buffer and to send another Continue-Message when Read-Ahead is turned off (no callback method).
iv. WpContinueRequestManager.ProcessContinueRequest method: It sets the Request state to SUCCEEDED and throws an exception when the very first parcel is 3115, 3116 or 3177 error and Read-Ahead is turned on (callback method).
v. WpStoredProcedureManager.ProcessSegmentResponse method: it invokes CheckForBufferOverflow method to resize the Response Buffer and to send another Continue-Message.
2- Error code 3115, 3116, and 3177 handled by Request Class: a. Request.MoveNext(Boolean) method: it detects 3115, 3116 or 3177 error parcel embedded within (at the end) of the Response Buffer. It reads the Error Parcel (and ErrorInfo parcel) first and later sends it to the GetNextBuffer method.
i. Request.SendContinueMessage method: it adjusts the Response Buffer Size when Error # is 3115, 3116 or 3177. It creates a WpContinueRequestManager object to send a Continue-Message to DBS. 1) Read-Ahead Turned On:
2) Read-Ahead Turned Off: WpContinueRequestManager will handle any additional Error 3115, 3116 or 3177. See bullet 1-III above.
b. Request.OnContinueComplete method: It will check TdException (if any) for error code 3115, 3116 or 3177. it invokes FillReadAheadBuffer method to re-send another Read-Ahead message. This corresponds to bullet 1-iv above. FillReadAheadBuffer invokes Request.SendContinueMessage method.
3- ParcelFactory.ReadAheadScan method: It scans the buffer looking for EndOfRequest (i.e. End of Stream) and Error (and associated ErrorInfo) Parcels. It assumes that Error 3115, 3116 or 3177 are the very end of the Response (last Error).
4- ParcelError.ShouldGrowResponseBuffer method: I added this method to PclError class so eventually we can centralize the logic in one place.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpRequestManager.SendAsyncAbort(System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Sends an asynchronous abort message to the DBS. This is used when:
The Request message was just sent and the user called TdCommand.Cancel(), which sets the Request.CancelRequest flag to true.
If the RequestTimeout is not infinite and a timer called this method after RequestTimeout. This is done to avoid setting the Socket.ReceiveTimeout with SslStream, which does not support it.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpStartRequestManager.ElicitDataManager
member.summary: This class is responsible for sending a single Lob parameter to the database. The ElicitDataManager always returns (calls back) the WpStartRequestManager when complete.

remarks.para: If the request is asynchronous, the Lob is sent synchronously, and all receive operations are performed asynchronously. After each send operation the LobState is validated and if the LOB_STATE is NO_MORE_DATA, the WpStartRequestManager RedriveAsyncAction(ManagerAction) is executed with an ActionManager.Receive.

If the request is synchronous, the Lob is sent and received synchronously. After each send operation the LobState is validated and if the LOB_STATE is NO_MORE_DATA, control is returned back to WpStartRequestManager ProcessRequestResponse().

member.summary: Sends the Start Request messages, process the response until the request is complete and we are awaiting the final response from Teradata. This includes sending all deferred parameter data.
member.remarks:
Step 1 : Execute receive Step 2 : Execute send and receive Step 3 : Execute send and receive while resending a request. The parameters are required to be reset before resending a request.

member.returns: True for deferred processing to continue

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpAbortRequestManager
member.summary: WpAbortRequestManager manages the wire protocol for aborting an active request.
member.remarks:
This is usually an asynchronous request from another thread (e.g. TdCommand.Cancel). The thread executing the query will read the response. If the request has encountered a timeout condition then the current thread must read the response to the abort request.
DBS does not guarantee that an ABORT will succeed (i.e. timing issues). Therefore ABORT message Response processing must be identical to the Start Request Message. Hence WpAbortRequestManager class derives from the WpStartRequestManager.

member.summary: Constructor for the WpAbortRequestManager. The Request object is supplying the buffer since we are reading the response from the DBS. The abort may or may not succeed, therefore, if the request does not get aborted, the Request buffer needs to contain the results of the successful query.

Receive the response synchronously from the DBS

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpAbortRequestManager.SentMessageKind
member.summary: Define the sent message kind method for the abort manager.

remarks.para: The abort manager may fail during a send, and continue to receive after reconnection for the request that had timed out. This allows for this condition, by providing the attempted last message sent from the abort request manager.

Without this override the SentMessageKind, which is set from the session will not contain a type, since the send failed. The ValidateResponseMessage would then return an invalid message kind exception.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpLanHeader
member.summary:
The Teradata LAN Message Header. This structure is at the beginning of all messages sent to/from Teradata. The LANHeader Format is as follows:
Field Size Offset Description ====================== ====== ====== ========================================== Version 1 byte 0 Wire protocol version Class 1 byte 1 Request or Response Kind 1 byte 2 COPKind of message HighOrderMessageLength 2 byte 3-4 High order bytes of 4 byte message length ByteVar 1 byte 5 Valid for Assign/Reassign requests WordVar 2 byte 6-7 Unused LowOrderMessageLength 2 byte 8-9 Low order bytes of 4 byte message length ReservedForExpansion 6 byte 10-15 Unused CorrelationTag 4 byte 16-19 Sent by client, returned by DBS SessionNumber 4 byte 20-23 DBS assigned session number Authentication 8 byte 24-31 Unique value per message, same value returned by DBS RequestNumber 4 byte 32-35 Client request number for Start requests GatewayByte 1 byte 36 Gateway capabilities HostCharSet 1 byte 37 Character set in use Padding 2 byte 38-39 Padding ControlDataLength 4 byte 40-43 Length of the Control Data if supported by DBS (14.10 or later) SpareBytes 8 byte 44-51 Unused

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSessionContext.SetDbsFeatures(Teradata.Client.Provider.PclConfigResponse)
member.summary: Set the DBS Features based on the config response parcel. The config response parcel indicates the features that are supported by DBS.

remarks.para: The default value for a DBS feature is false. The config response parcel turns the flag on for DBS version that support the feature. Hence increasing DBS versions start enabling more flags. Therefore it is safe to use the config response parcel for all DBS version, because the default feature value is false if the feature flag is not present in the config response parcel.

The context initialization is a 3 step process: 1) Initialize the context in the constructor. 2) Set the DBS features from the config response 3) Set the DBS Version, the DBS Limits and the Session Options.

member.summary: Represents the physical Teradata session state

Connected: Socket connection to Teradata is open and the initial user authentication (round-trips) have taken place.
Disconnected: Socket connection to Teradata is closed.

State transitions: Initialized to Connected or Disposed. Connected to Disconnected Disconnected to Disposed or Initialized??? Connected to Reconnecting Reconnecting to Disconnecting Reconnecting to Connected

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession._messageGateStatus
member.summary: Indicates the status of the Message Gate.
member.remarks:
An Other Message is a message other than a Start or Abort Message.
An Other Message will never close the gate. Only one Start Message is allowed inside the gate. Once a Start Message passes through the gate, the gate will be shut until the Start Message has been processed.
MsgGateStatus.MessageGateOpen -- gate is open MsgGateStatus.MessageGateClosed -- gate is closed

member.name: F:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession._waitForMsgGateEvent
member.summary: Manual wait handle that is used when a Message must wait for the message gate to open.
member.remarks:
Since the EventWaitHandle is manual, once it gets signaled all threads waiting will be released.
There is a situation when a "busy session" exception cannot be thrown back to the application when the Message gate is closed. This occurs when an application calls BeginExecuteNonQuery to process a SELECT statement. In this situation the provider skips all the rows generated by the SELECT. To skip the rows, it must go through all the rows. It is possible that the provider will need to send a CONTINUE messages to retrieve the next buffer full of data. If the Message Gate is closed, the provider must wait for it to open before proceeding.

member.name: P:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession.IsConnected
member.summary: Indicates if the WpSession is connected.
member.remarks: Previously this property called into the WpTransport isConnected property, which returns the socket state. member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession.Reconnect(System.Int32)
member.summary: Reconnect the session.
member.exception: The session cannot be reconnected. Refer to the InnerException for more information.
member.returns: RedriveInfo that contains the information needed to decide whether request(s) can be redriven
member.remarks:
If an error/failure is returned from Teradata that is not expected, the session will be considered to be not reconnect-able.
The following errors are not reconnect-able: 8055 -- Session forced off by PMPC or GtwGlobal or security violation This will occur when the session is killed from GtwGlobal. It will appear as the inner exception to TeraGSS Security Library error 115022 when encryption is turned on. 8018 -- The session id is illegal This error gets thrown if the reconnection does not occur with 20 minutes of a disconnection from the database. After 20 minutes the gateway performs a cleanup of unconnected connections. 3134 -- The request was aborted by an ABORT SESSION command. This will occur when the session is Killed from AbortSession UDF.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession.BeginTransmit(Teradata.Client.Provider.WpSession.MessageType,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Used to start the transmission of Messages to Teradata. Method will check the status of the Message gate and wait on EventHandle until it has been set.
member.param: The message type that is going to be submitted
Indicates that caller wants to wait for the Message Gate to open: true==wait for open, false==busy exception will be thrown
member.remarks:
The message types are as follows: NoopMessage -- no messages StartMessage -- start message AbortMessage -- abort message OtherMessage -- other type of messages not including start and abort.
There is a scenario where an exception will NOT be thrown if the Message Gate is closed. This will occur when a Continue Message is sent going through the result set of a SELECT that was executed by BeginExecuteNonQuery/ExecuteNonQuery. In this case, the thread sending the Continue Message will wait until the Message Gate is open. This is indicated by setting the waitForMsgGateOpen parameter to true.
waitForMsgGate = true is only applicable to an Other Message.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpTcpTransport
member.summary: The class implements the IWpTransport interface using TCP/IP for the transport protocol.
member.remarks: IMPORTANT NOTE: The Asynchronous Receive (i.e. BeginReceive) invokes the callback (to higher levels i.e. Message Managers) when OnReceiveComplete is invoked by the socket. This means that the another thread can reach WpTcpTransport before the original thread returns from OnReceiveComplete method. Therefore the overall State (all fields, locks, Synchronization objects and etc.) must be finalized before higher levels are notified by invoking the callback.

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpTcpTransport.SetDesiredPorts(System.Int32@,System.Nullable{System.Int32}@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Based on _useTls and _sslMode sets: (a) the primary and secondary ports to be used with LCC to establish the connection, and (b) the maximum number of sockets that can be used concurrently.

remarks.para: _useTls is null until we get , , or we determine from PCLGTWCONFIGPORTS that we connected to the wrong port.
Once the connection is successful, will set _useTls to indicate which port was connected (to true for HTTPS and false for unencrypted).

list.item: if _useTls == true, then primaryPort = _httpsPort, secondaryPort = null
if _useTls == false, then primaryPort = _unencryptedPort, secondaryPort = null

if _useTls == null and
_sslMode == Disable, then primaryPort = _unencryptedPort, secondaryPort = null
_sslMode == Allow, then primaryPort = _unencryptedPort, secondaryPort = _httpsPort
_sslMode == Prefer, then primaryPort = _httpsPort, secondaryPort = _unencryptedPort
_sslMode in (Require, Verify-CA, Verify-Full), then primaryPort = _httpsPort, secondaryPort = null

member.name: M:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpTcpTransport.OnReceiveComplete(System.IAsyncResult)
member.summary: Callback method that will be called when the Socket BeginReceive call has completed.
member.param: The IAsyncResult created by the Socket.BeginReceive call
member.remarks:
At this point we have completed a Partial asynchronous Socket receive of the LAN Header. Since all Teradata messages come immediately after the LAN header, the rest of the message should be available to read. Therefore, we complete the next read operation synchronously since the data should be immediately available. Since the Receive() method call returns a reference to a WpLanHeader, we create a private field to hold that reference. The WpLanHeader is then returned when the caller calls EndReceive.
IMPORTANT NOTE: The Asynchronous Receive (i.e. BeginReceive) invokes the callback (to higher levels i.e. Message Managers) when OnReceiveComplete is invoked by the socket. This means that the another thread can reach WpTcpTransport before the original thread returns from OnReceiveComplete method. Therefore the overall State (all fields, locks, Synchronization objects and etc.) must be finalized before higher levels are notified by invoking the callback.

member.name: T:Teradata.Client.Provider.WpTcpTransport.WpDataSourceResolver
member.summary: WpDataSourceResolver encapsulates the logic for resolving IP Addresses for a DataSource. This is also known as COP-Discovery.
member.remarks:
There is one WpDataSourceResolver instance per DataSource+DataSourceDnsEntries. This way, multiple threads can share the information that have already been cached.
There are three lookup algorithms based on the DataSourceDnsEntries connection string property.
a) DataSourceDnsEntries = 0 OR DataSource = 111.222.333.444 COP entries are not defined in DNS for each node. DNS is invoked to resolve the DataSource. This allows DNS based load balancing to be used. Data Provider will connect to the IP-Addresses in sequence as returned by DNS.
b) DataSourceDnsEntries > 0 COP entries are defined in DNS for each node. Primary COP: A random number is selected between 1 and DataSourceDnsEntries. Each subsequent lookup/connection will increment to the next node/COP number in a circular fashion. Therefore the Primary COP is selected in round-robin fashion. The remaining COPs (not Primary COP) are assigned to Failover-COP-list which is shuffled.
C) DataSourceDnsEntries = -1 (undefined) Data Provider will begin with COP1. Data Provider will continue to increment the COP number until a DNS lookup fails. At this point DataSourceDnsEntries is known; the remaining process is identical to "DataSourceDnsEntries > 0". DataSourceDnsEntries is set to Zero when COP1 lookup fails to return an IP address.
